items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由内罗毕新厂牌 Cool Waters 发行，是德国籍肯尼亚驻地打击乐手 Sven Kacirek 与两位本土音乐人 Ogoya Nengo 和 Olith Ratengo 的首次三方合作。Kacirek 与 Ratengo 组成的 Odd Okoddo 自 2018 年起活跃，此次加入八十三岁的肯尼亚东部传统 dodo 唱法歌手 Nengo，为作品注入深厚的传统根基。Kacirek 以 Buchla 合成器、手掌打击乐和套鼓构建层叠的合成复节奏，低调地衬托人声而不掩盖传统根源。《Bara》从简单的重复击打声起，逐步引入 4/4 节拍、流动低音和木琴质感，多层元素在曲终时显得浑然一体。《Sarah》则以 Ratengo 主导的演唱配合 Kacirek 试探性打击声响，失真效果在人声高潮处精准切入。评论指出，Nengo 与 Ratengo 因住所相邻而共享的根脉，以及跨国跨代的合作模式，使古老的肯尼亚传统在当代电子语境中焕发新生，成为非洲与全球文化对话的范例。

Francesco Paolo Paladi
items.body: Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release, Under an Endless Sky . In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari, Songs of Compassion is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics. Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari | Photo by Maria Assunta Karini Songs of Compassion has two challenges for the listener. The first is the music, called variously avant-garde, ambient, modal, non-linear, and a few more. It is played mostly on pianos mixed in and out of the foreground, sometimes doubled, and sometimes out of phase, joined by strings, woodwinds, synth washes, and steely sounds. Initially disorienting, the music serves to remind us how locked our minds are to Western notions of harmonic movement. It speaks of alternative musical narratives much older and much further away. They are songs that subvert the song: more like Steve Reich than Steve Stills; more like Phillip Glass than Phil Collins. UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY - Pale Wanderer At the same time, there are the poetic yet strikingly contemporary lyrics. �Pale Wanderer� talks about the fact that authoritarianism needs willing accomplices, describing what happens �When you make a deal with darkness.� UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY (Dorothy Moskowitz, Francesco Paolo Paladino e Luka Chino Ferrari) by Silentes �Charlottesville� (written with the late Joe Byrd) evokes the time not long ago when torch-wielding nazis, proud of the metaphoric Ns on their tunics, chanted the antisemitic tropes paraphrased in Moskowitz�s words, �We�ll be one people, pure of race/No greedy throng could take our place� . Besides the overtly political lyrics, in the tradition of 1960s protest songs, there are also thoughtful meditations on mortality and our place in the universe. The message is high-minded yet sincere and direct. World weary and wise, Moskowitz�s voice inhabits the evocative philosophical lyrics with the authority of a skilled method actor. The melodies unfold like streams of consciousness, rising and falling, not following expected diatonic chord progressions, but honouring, instead, the value of each word. Moskowitz�s piano acts as another voice and sometimes a kind of Greek chorus commenting on the proceedings. The surrounding music frames, creates pulses and dissonances, and shimmers. The return of Dorothy Moskowitz with her renamed project has arrived in a moment quite similar to the times that spawned its predecessor. Political division, unrest, and uncertainty always generate artistic reaction, and United States of Alchemy roared back to life with their epic 24-minute opening track �Under an Endless Sky� in 2023, serving perhaps as an �In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida� for our times. Songs of Compassion continues to challenge how we think about our world. It�s music that defies the song form, while doing exactly what music is supposed to do�enrich the human condition. Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: Dorothy Moskowitz 与合作者 Francesco Paolo Paladino、Luca Chino Ferrari 在专辑《Songs of Compassion》中构建了一套非线性的声音世界。音乐以钢琴为核心，辅以弦乐、木管、合成器声场与金属质感音色，呈现出模态化、空间化的结构，刻意打破西方和声运动的惯性思维。评论将其比作 Steve Reich 与 Philip Glass 的延续——旋律如意识流般起伏，不依赖传统功能和声，而是服务于每个词的意义。Moskowitz 的嗓音苍老而权威，既承担哲学化的歌词表达，又作为方法派演员般赋予文字以重量。歌词层面，专辑既延续1960年代抗议歌曲传统，直面威权主义与法西斯回潮等政治议题，也深入对死亡与人类在宇宙中位置的冥想。整体呈现出高密度的前卫实验与严肃社会关怀的交织。

items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. Find the artist online. Further reading: Tako Toki - Hirsute Farfelus (Review) Terje Isungset - Glacial Poetry (Review)

items.body: Sendas by Omar Sosa True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa�s Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. As with all Sosa�s work, Sendas is the fortunate product of serendipity. In 2021 the COVID lockdown was underway, his marriage was ending, and a scheduled Milan appearance cancellation garnered an invitation to record at the Fazioli Pianoforti Concert Hall, annex to the renowned Italian piano manufactory in Sacile, Pordenone, about an hour northeast of Venice. At Fazioli, Sosa found himself in august company. Herbie Hancock and a host of classical pianists are Fazioli artists. Among the institutions that have embraced the Fazioli sound are the Juilliard School, Teatro La Fenice (Venice), the Budapest Palace of Arts, the Paris Conservatory, the Beijing Grand Theatre, and the universities of Salzburg, Graz, and Vienna. An unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in the empty concert hall provided the raw audio for Sendas , later to be flavored in the mix, sparsely, with voice clips, percussion, loops, field recordings, found sounds effects that Sosa has collected over a career spanning four decades. As Sosa related to me soon after completing the post-production of Sendas , �Humanity is spiritually lost. We humans are all in this together. We need to evolve, but always keeping the traditions, walking with a strong, determined pace. We need more grounded music with overtones that resonate with the lower chakras� like throat singing, a mantra of the universal music.� �Creativity is about combining all your influences in a new way. I don�t aspire to be jazz, Latin, timba, reggaeton, classical. I avoid styles, but I respect the forms.� �I try not to think about how listeners will receive it but I do try to address their expectations, and go with the music to some other new place. Many free spirits come to listen, to be a part of the journey we are on.� Sosa laughs, �My son says, �Your niche is really small.� But the people who come really are there to be part of what we are going to do.� �Economics, technology, the streaming ear wash, algorithms all want to put you into a defined category � and so do many music journalists! The industry�s mentality is that any investment in artists must be defined by market categories to be profitable.� �But I play to be free of that,� Sosa says. �I play without thinking. There are no wrong notes. I love the first take. That�s the take, the natural voice of your soul. �Less is more� is a mantra in my life and music.� Consider the opening of �Inside the Spirit,� easing in leisurely, reaching over the keyboard into the resonant heart of the instrument, plucking and stroking the strings, teasing out a fuller resonance � only later to be embellished in the studio mix with light percussion and the muted Spanish-language refrain of a pregonero or street vendor, as might be heard in the calles of Havana or any other Latin American barrio. Sendas by Omar Sosa Moving from the secular to the sacred, �Deities Serenade� is an Afro-Cuban invocation of the shape-shifting divine, yet with ample room for ecumenical recasting in accord with a listener�s own self-location. �Inside My Soul� and �Something from Home� are Sosa works that to my ear may be an intuitive response to the distant call of Chopin�s "Nocturnes," to which Sosa says he listened every night for two years as a conservatory student in Cuba. Sendas by Omar Sosa �Caribbean Movement� and �Shirma� speak to Sosa�s rootedness in the lyrical, rhythmic, and harmonic heritage of the plantation islands where African and European cultures tragically entwined. In the violent forging of the world�s first truly modern people, social, cultural, linguistic, and musical displacements proved more flexible and accommodating than many of those same people, who shaped a contentious convergence of traditions into a changing same that persists into the unfolding present, ever yet to come. With expressive transcendence such as this, seeking to reduce the spiritual essence and inspiration of Sosa�s music to words is rather a fool�s errand. Better rather to listen, to contemplate, to perceive the pathway, to wander the sonic sendas coursing to the next way station without prejudice or preconception. To that end, Scott Price, Sosa�s longtime manager and friend relates, �We are using Sendas as the springboard for our first experiments in AI-generated Omar Sosa music videos.� Absent the opportunity to see and hear Sosa perform live, the palpable ideal, these ancillary audiovisual experiments further the ineffability of his artistic quest, the unique nature of the listening experience and all that ensues.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是古巴钢琴家Omar Sosa在意大利Fazioli音乐厅进行的两小时无脚本独奏即兴录音，经后期混音处理，加入稀疏的人声片段、打击乐、循环音效、田野录音与拾得声响。Sosa延续了对Thelonious Monk'绝不重复'理念的致敬，专辑诞生于新冠封锁期间，融合了他跨越四十年的多元影响——爵士、拉丁、蒂姆巴、雷鬼顿、古典元素共存却拒绝被任何风格标签框定。他在创作中强调'少即是多'与'没有错误的音符'，追求首遍录音的自然灵魂之声。后期制作中以轻盈打击乐与人声采样点缀，营造冥想氛围，呼应他对'根基性音乐'与低脉轮泛音的追求。这张作品展现了不受算法与市场分类束缚的自由精神，是一位进化中艺术家的沉思记录。

items.body: In “Rokia”, a young villager falls in love with his neighbour, and her mother, Rokia, opposes the relationship. Rabie Houti, a violinist and singer from Oran in Algeria who has lived in Montpellier since 2014, tells the story with Gasba Électrique, who combine Maghrebi flute with electronic textures. The track brings together his Arabo-Andalusian violin, electronic beats and rock guitars, and builds gradually into a trance. Trance is the band’s own word for its live shows too, which have taken them from Montpellier to Canada, Algeria and Kazakhstan. Houti’s own road to those stages started in Oran, where his father loved Arabo-Andalusian music and his older sister Khedija taught him his first notes on a mandolin. Around the age of eight he played his first concert, on violin, with the junior orchestra of the Nassim El Andalous school at Oran’s opera house. These days he leads the Rabie Houti Band, active since 2017, who set Maghrebi melodies over funk and rock grooves and place themselves in “Sono Mondiale”, the movement the late Rachid Taha championed. Joudour, their second album, takes its title from the Arabic word for roots, and the band marked its release with a free show at Rockstore in Montpellier on 3 October. It follows Tahtaha from 2019, which Houti describes as a test from a time when the band was still searching; with Joudour, he says, they found their signature. The new album leans further into rock and electronics, and every track is an original composition. You can stream “Rokia” and Joudour HERE. The post Daily Discovery: Rabie Houti – Rokia appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._genre: Arabo-Andalusian / Maghrebi fusion / electronic / world fusion
items._cn_summary: Rabie Houti 是一位来自阿尔及利亚奥兰的小提琴手兼歌手，现居蒙彼利埃。他的乐队 Gasba Électrique 将马格里布长笛与电子音色结合，作品融合阿拉伯-安达卢西亚小提琴、电子节拍与摇滚吉他，逐步构建出迷 trance 般的氛围。Houti 出身于奥兰的音乐世家，父亲热爱阿拉伯-安达卢西亚音乐，姐姐教他弹奏曼陀林，八岁便在歌剧院与青少年乐团合作演出。乐队自 2017 年活跃至今，自定位为已故 Rachid Taha 所倡导的「Sono Mondiale」运动的延续，将马格里布旋律置于放克与摇滚律动之上。2025 年发行的第二张专辑《Joudour》（阿拉伯语意为「根」）相较首作《Tahtaha》进一步深化摇滚与电子融合，每首曲目均为原创，展现了乐队在融合探索中找到的标志性声音。

items.body: Sydney-based producer Harry Klein released the single “Fleeting Moments” in 2026, a dark-pop track built from electronica, wave and witch house. The song centers on transience, and on learning to love what doesn’t last. “Fleeting Moments” runs 3:22 and carries a synthesized trumpet line, falsetto vocals and a glitch beat. The single adds to a run of 2026 releases that includes “Push and Pull,” “Only Ever Now,” “Dance Therapy,” “Sun Down” featuring Billsbry, “Wild Child” and “Refuge” featuring Just Jen. Klein is touring Europe with psych-jazz outfit Almost Toast and plans to release his second album, “On The Path,” in November 2026 after he returns to Sydney. Rex Pollard of Electronic Music Australia described Klein’s production in terms of the mood it builds: “It is clear to me that Klein contains excellent knowledge on formulating dystopian atmospheres with his production, encouraging listeners to exit reality and enter his dark, sinister worlds.” “Fleeting Moments” is available to stream on Spotify. About Harry Klein Harry Klein is a multidisciplinary artist based in Eora/Sydney who combines music production with visual artistry across audio/visual performances. His work moves through dark electronica, glitchy IDM beats and ambient textures. Klein released his debut album, “And Then There Was None,” in 2023. The record explores questions of relationships, community and social power, pairing experimental electronica and dance productions with melancholic pop songwriting. Three singles preceded it that year: “Running out of Time,” “Cut & Dirty” and “Accelerate,” followed later in 2023 by “Who Floats Above.” He has performed at Up Late at the Powerhouse Museum and the Brand X Artist Showcase, built an interactive sound installation at Wide Open Space Festival, played his festival debut at Waves Retreat Festival and collaborated with fashion label The Injury at Pitch Festival. Klein also works as Senior Technical Officer of Screen Arts and Photomedia at Sydney College of the Arts, where he teaches and mentors emerging artists. “Fleeting Moments” is the latest in a string of 2026 singles building toward “On The Path,” Klein’s second album, due in November 2026.
items._genre: dark-pop / electronica / witch house / wave / glitch
items._cn_summary: Harry Klein 来自悉尼，是一位跨领域艺术家，将音乐制作与视觉艺术结合于音画演出中。2026年发行的单曲《Fleeting Moments》以电子合成小号线、假声人声与故障节拍构建出阴郁氛围，主题围绕短暂性与不可持存之物展开。该曲延续其首张专辑《And Then There Was None》对关系、社群与社会权力议题的探索路径，将实验电子与暗潮质感融入忧郁流行结构。他即将在欧洲与psyche-jazz乐队Almost Toast一同巡演，并计划于十一月发行第二张专辑《On The Path》。其制作擅长制造反乌托邦声场，将听众引入黑暗而诡谲的听觉空间，同时保持流行可听性。

items.body: Claudio Dondo began making music in the late 1980s. This path eventually led him to Runes Order, the project under which he has released countless recordings on a wide variety of labels since 1992. He has now joined forces with the German label Dark Vinyl Records and, much like on his previous album, initiated a collaboration with Regen Graves. We are presented with a total of 13 tracks. While the influences are highly eclectic, they can largely be categorized within genres such as Cinematic and Krautrock. The inclusion of additional guest musicians adds further diversity—for instance, on one track, a saxophone creates a wonderfully dark, Jazzy atmosphere. I wasn’t surprised to find references to John Carpenter’s films, yet this album offers far more than just Cinematic soundscapes. From vintage drum machine tones to driving rhythms, and from organ passages to analog effects, this work has a great deal to offer. Add to this a variety of vocal tracks alongside the instrumentals, and the result is a fascinating work that keeps the listener firmly in its grip. This is a varied and accomplished opus containing a few real gems. (Rating:7½). Listen to “Bury The Fetus”: Bury The Fetus by Runes Order & Regen Graves About Runes Order & Regen Graves Runes Order & Regen Graves is the collaboration between Claudio Dondo’s long-running Italian dark ambient project Runes Order, based in the Genoa area, and Regen Graves, a musician from the same Genoa scene known as a member of the horror-doom band Abysmal Grief. Dondo started the project in 1988 as Order 1968 and renamed it Runes Order in 1992 with the cassette “The Dream Door”. His catalogue includes “La Seduzione Del Silenzio” (1994), “Room 39” (1995), “The Art of Scare and Sorrow” (2002) and “Fase XIV” (2019), drawing on the cosmic and Berlin School tradition of Tangerine Dream, Faust and Klaus Schulze. Dondo and Regen Graves first joined forces on “Falsche Fragen” in 2023. “Escape”, their second album together, followed in 2026 on Dark Vinyl Records, pairing Berlin School electronics with horror and thriller soundtrack atmospheres across the thirteen tracks reviewed here.
items._genre: dark ambient / cinematic / krautrock / electronic
items._cn_summary: 意大利音乐人Claudio Dondo自1980年代末开始创作，1992年起以Runes Order之名持续推出作品。此次他与来自同一热那亚地下场景、同时也是恐怖末日金属乐队Abysmal Grief成员的Regen Graves合作，在德国小众厂牌Dark Vinyl Records发行第二张合作专辑《Escape》，共收录13首曲目。专辑将柏林学派的电子技法与恐怖及惊悚电影配乐氛围相结合，跨越暗黑氛围、Krautrock与电影音乐等风格边界。客座乐手的加入进一步丰富了层次，其中萨克斯管的运用为部分曲目注入了阴郁而爵士化的气息。从复古鼓机音色到推进感强烈的节奏段落，从风琴段落到模拟合成器效果，再到人声与器乐作品的交替安排，整张专辑在结构与音色上展现出相当的多样性。乐评将其定位为一部变化丰富且完成度高的作品，其中包含若干真正出色的亮点段落。

items.body: Progressive rock can be defined in many ways but one of my favorites is with the tension between a frenetic, jittery energy and sweet, soothing melody. Think King Crimson, where you never know which the band will choose from and often get both: the staccato, chopped up riff, or the dreamy, pleasing melody. This creates a tension, a contrast between the two sounds that, when wielded well, generates an inimitable energy and mood. Sans Froid are experts at doing just that, marrying dense, complex, unpredictable instrumentation and unexpected vocal phrases with a "classic" melodic approach. The end result is Back Into the Womb, an album that covers the spaces between heavy, muscular progressive rock and fragile, warm art rock."Go On", the track which opens the album, leaves us very little space before it introduces the first aspect of this sound. This is the track's excellent combo of the main guitar riff, punchy drums, and punctual bass. It creates that off-kilter vibe I mentioned earlier, that jittery feeling. The vocals follow suit but also quickly usher in the other mood, a more classical, melodic kind of approach on the track's first bridge. But here's the thing - that back and forth is not maintained. There is no A/B/A/B/C structure to this track. It gets smashed to pieces by this sudden turn that the instruments and especially the vocals take around at two minutes and fifteen. It's hard to overstate how much I love what happens there: the initially repetitive but then exquisitely explosive vocals, the deconstructed guitar line, and then the return of the big, muscular main riff.The entire album is filled with these ideas, refusing to choose one style and instead hopping between groove, experimentation, emotiveness, abrasiveness and more. Throughout, the vocals lead the way. They're incredible, again channeling that contrast we opened on. Their basic timbre is very sweet but it often gets augmented by a throaty, full approach that works exceedingly well with the album's basic groove. But, as evinced on "Go On", Sans Froid are happy to manipulate them further, sometimes casting them in sweeping, "traditional" choruses and sometimes chopping them up and deploying them in non-standard ways while at others setting them as a melancholic, emotive, gentle dirge. The result is that their sound is the centerpiece of the album, tying everything together, but never becoming obvious or background noise.Which also brings us, at the outset, full circle to the album's other brilliance: its production. Every instrument is meticulously placed where it needs to be and even on the album's busiest passages, every comes through beautifully. The bass is at the bottom but it never slips, always audible in its support. The drums hit very hard right where they should without overwhelming anything else. And the guitars are at time noisy and beefy but at others poignantly sharp and incisiveness. It serves to bring Sans Froid's ambition, which is substantial, to exquisite execution, bringing forth the musical vision in beautiful light. Fans of progressive rock know how hard this is to achieve and also know the joy of discovering an album which does this well, an intricate album whose sound matches its composition. Back Into the Womb is that and more, an album from a band which I knew nothing about that does everything I love progressive rock for. Back into the Womb by Sans Froid
items._genre: progressive rock / experimental / art rock
items._cn_summary: 专辑在密集复杂、不可预测的器乐编排与温暖人声之间制造强烈张力，体现出前卫摇滚的实验内核。从开场曲即以切分吉他、强劲鼓点与精准贝斯构建不稳态律动，随后在两分十五秒处突然转向解构式人声与爆发性编排，彻底打破常规A/B段落结构。全作拒绝单一风格，在律动、即兴、情绪化与粗粝感之间自由跳跃。人声是核心纽带——甜美音色与沙哑唱法交替出现，时而以传统合唱形式呈现，时而碎片化处理，或化作忧郁挽歌。制作方面，每件乐器都经过精细的空间定位，即使在最密集段落也层次分明。贝斯稳固支撑低频，鼓击恰到好处，吉他在粗砺与锐利间灵活转换，整体服务于乐队的艺术构想。

items.body: Look at all those people! Everything seems bigger on Hour‘s newest album. There are fourteen people in the ensemble (four missing the photo shoot). The Bandcamp description is a thousand words long. The album is offered on black vinyl, colored vinyl, deluxe CD and promo CD. So why does Ghost Bridge sound so much smaller and more intimate ~ even more so than Subminiature? The answers are the arrangements and the brevity. On Ghost Bridge, the Philly ensemble led by Michael Cormier-O’Leary continues its slow shift from post-rock to modern composition. The pieces – and by extension, the instruments – are given more room to breathe. A half dozen tracks unfold in a concise 36 minutes. Late in the set, a vocal selection slows the pace to a pleasant crawl. Hour is still more Rachel’s than Low, but is carving out a niche at a pace similar to that of a stream cutting channels in stone. The title is taken from an “unrealized movie concept” about a disappearing and reappearing bridge. From this prompt, the album muses on tragedies, ghosts and the nature of the soul. Over a quarter of the album is devoted to the title track, whose very length suggests it bears the specter of post-rock. Solo piano is joined by light drums, then vibraphone, then all the other instruments in time, gathering like a crowd at a wake, forming layers of consolation, adding confidence and strength until the grief itself becomes a ghost. The end is a soft mist of notes, a few stragglers staying behind to whisper to the piano before they all go home. But where did it all begin? “Pearls” is the opening track, proceeding from a series of repeated notes to engage in happy permutations. Little sorrow can be intuited here; instead the starting point is a breezy, carefree day, filled with horse-drawn carriages and hot air balloons until the full stop at the three-minute mark, when darker clouds can be seen on the horizon: not yet here, but on their way. The pianist stumbles; the string players look up; the concentration of the percussionist is disrupted. The flautist resets the mood: the sorrow has not yet approached, so let us savor the now. The sedate ending sets up “Centralia,” a series of layered phrases that circle back and repeat like recurring thoughts or the motivational sentences of friends. Only after “Ghost Bridge” does “Sky Is Blue” emerge, perfectly placed as the first track on Side B, albeit jarring in the digital and CD versions. The lyrics, sung by Heeyoon Won, reveal it to be an extensive message from the great beyond, delivered by a loved one who is completely okay, filled with perspective, encouragement and hope. Should one not own the LP, we recommend moving “Sky Is Blue” to the finale. Given this sequencing, “So Long Without a Word” slips into the void at the end of “Ghost Bridge,” its melodic tones speaking directly to the soul, the full stop now at 2:00, followed by increasing energy and resolve. A third phase begins two minutes later with insistent, cinematic strums, then a playful series of shifts, jazz to chamber and back, like a playground ball. “Sonny” returns the timbre to post-rock and the mood to reflective yet ebullient, the ghost bridge now reappearing, the path between heaven and earth secure. (Richard Allen)
items._genre: modern composition / post-rock / contemporary classical
items._cn_summary: Hour 乐团由十四人组成，在三十七分钟内以六首作品呈现从后摇向现代作曲的过渡。专辑标题源自一部关于消失与重现之桥的未实现电影构想，由此引申出对悲剧、幽灵与灵魂本质的沉思。独奏钢琴首先响起，鼓与颤音琴逐层加入，其余乐器如守灵现场的人群般汇聚，形成层层慰藉的声部堆积，最终消散于朦胧的余韵。开场曲从反复音型展开轻快的变奏，三分钟后骤停，预示暗云将至。整张专辑在编曲上给予乐器充分的呼吸空间，段落简洁克制，人声曲目作为唯一带有歌词的段落，传递来自远方的安慰讯息。整体氛围内敛沉思，介于器乐后摇的缓慢铺陈与现代室内乐的精致结构之间。

items.body: Two decades removed from the clockwork IDM of Polytuft-Tech, Tim Martin’s returning light (Home Normal) and beneath still stars (handstitched*) find him stripping everything back to drift, texture, and quietly resonant melody, resulting in two companion albums that feel less like separate releases than different sides of the same long, unhurried thought.   Companion pieces, two sides of the same drift beneath still stars by maps and diagrams returning light by maps and diagrams   Tim Martin has been Maps and Diagrams since the early 2000s, and the entry point for a lot of people into his catalog is Polytuft-Tech, released in 2003 on Expanding Records, an album that got filed under IDM, ambient, and glitch at a moment when those three words together still meant something specific and rigorous. That record ran on clicky drums that whirred like clockwork under warm, streamlined melodies. It landed near the tail end of IDM’s most experimentally saturated period, right as the genre itself was quietly transitioning into whatever came next, and it stands as one of the more melodically generous statements from that stretch. Both returning light (Home Normal) and beneath still stars (handstitched*) are nowhere near that record sonically. Drums are gone almost entirely. Glitch has been replaced by drift. But it’s still unmistakably Tim, the same restrained, resonant signature that’s followed him through two decades of output, just aged into something quieter. Both albums arrive within weeks of each other on different labels with different histories attached. returning light is Home Normal‘s second release from Tim this year, following tone isolation, his actual debut on the label despite Home Normal running for over seventeen years, a gap explained by the fact that Tim‘s earliest UK work went through Nomadic Kids Republic, Home Normal‘s sister label, back in 2011 with Lights Will Call On You and The Town Beneath The Sea. beneath still stars comes out on handstitched*, the label Tim runs himself, which has carried his more private and experimental output for years alongside releases like In Circles. One album through someone else’s curatorial lens, one through his own. That distinction matters more than it initially seems to. Ambient releases should never get judged track by track in isolation. The genre works as a collective experience, an album like this either builds a sustained emotional environment across its runtime or it doesn’t, and no individual piece can really save or sink that outcome on its own. What matters more is whether the melodies that surface actually resonate, whether they invoke something specific rather than just occupying space. Both of these records succeed at that, though they do it through slightly different means. “ArcWorld-6.4 Rev.42 [sgl.break]” from beneath still stars is one of the more fascinating pieces across either release, another example of the part A / part B structure that’s shown up in other reviews recently. It connects two ideas without part B ever feeling like a continuation of part A. Instead it functions as an introduction to something entirely different, and the transition is peaceful in a way that most of this album is. The track titles throughout beneath still stars read almost like technical drafts, numbered revisions, hertz values, file extensions in brackets like [static] or [lost.wav] or [mem.void]. That naming isn’t arbitrary. It reads like an iteration system, drafts selected and refined specifically rather than titled decoratively after the fact. “Raddius.ocean-IX [r.36-04hz]” is another two-part piece, but this one connects rather than diverges, a drone-like melodic note giving way to a dreamlike synth tuned to a specific frequency, which the title tells you outright. Intentional down to the hertz. “beneath still stars and returning light aren’t competing statements, they’re companion pieces, two sides of the same drift, released close enough together that they start to feel like one long, unhurried thought that just happened to get split across two labels.” ~J. Batista A different level of drone entirely :: returning light sits in the same emotional register but sounds noticeably different sonically. There are small clicks and glitches scattered through certain tracks, and the pads and atmospheres carry a different weight than what’s happening on beneath still stars. “falling rainbows” uses static hits inside its pad environments to create reverbed textures that read almost like snare hits, except Tim‘s building that rhythmic tension entirely out of pad effects and reverb rather than anything resembling a drum sample. “just moving” introduces keys that sound almost like distortion at first before resolving into something prettier the longer you sit with it, a different level of drone entirely, since nothing here holds on a single note. There’s room for other melodies to form and enter, and they do. “somewhat virtual interactions” is a favorite, what sounds like a distorted “ahhh” vocal fragment sits so subtly in the mix that it changes the character of the pads around it, and there are field recording glitches scattered throughout that open up real space inside the track. “Open Water” plays almost like an audio representation of a shishi-odoshi—that traditional Japanese bamboo water fountain that fills, tips, empties, and resets in a slow repeating cycle. Tim‘s using effects here the same way that device uses gravity and water, building a soft, cyclical sense of rhythm entirely out of texture rather than percussion. “ouvertures” closes the album starting soft and distorted, and around the 3:55 mark a low humming frequency starts creeping in that sounds baked into the synth itself, eventually rolling and degrading the audio as the track winds down. A genuinely cool effect to end on. “Tim Martin has landed somewhere his younger self probably wasn’t building toward. Whether that’s evolution or just where two decades of making ambient music eventually deposits a person is hard to say, and probably doesn’t matter.” ~J. Batista There’s a version of this review that picks a favorite between the two records. That version would be missing the point entirely. beneath still stars and returning light aren’t competing statements, they’re companion pieces, two sides of the same drift, released close enough together that they start to feel like one long, unhurried thought that just happened to get split across two labels. beneath still stars is the more clinical of the pair. Drafted, revised, numbered like lab notes, every track title reading like a version history for a synth that never stops evolving. Twenty years removed from Polytuft-Tech‘s clockwork drums and whirring percussion, Tim Martin has landed somewhere his younger self probably wasn’t building toward. Whether that’s evolution or just where two decades of making ambient music eventually deposits a person is hard to say, and probably doesn’t matter. These two records don’t argue for themselves. They don’t need to. They just sit there, patiently, until you notice forty minutes have passed and you’ve barely moved. Home Normal got the warmer half. handstitched*—Tim‘s own label, his own house, got the rawer, more exacting one. He gets to have it both ways. So does anyone who sits with both records long enough to stop telling them apart. beneath still stars is available on handstitched* and returing light is available on Home Normal. beneath still stars by maps and diagrams returning light by maps and diagramsThe post [2View] Maps and Diagrams’ beneath still stars (handstitched*) & returning light (Home Normal) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.

items._cn_summary: Tim Martin以Maps and Diagrams之名活跃二十余年，早期作品Polytuft-Tech属于IDM与glitch范畴，带有节拍驱动的精密结构。此次两张专辑《returning light》与《beneath still stars》几乎完全剥离了节奏元素，回归drift、texture与安静旋律的ambient语汇。两张作品分别通过Home Normal与自创厂牌handstitched*发行，一张经他人策展视野过滤，一张保留私密实验色彩。评论强调ambient应以整体情感氛围而非单曲成败来评判，两张专辑在旋律浮现时均能唤起具体的情感共振。《beneath still stars》中的"ArcWorld-6.4 Rev.42 [sgl.break]"被特别提及，展现出更引人入胜的一面。整体从IDM到ambient的二十年蜕变呈现出节制、深沉的个人美学。

items.body: Neubauten's uncompromising debut album ‘Kollaps’ is 45 years old. Jeremy Allen explores the bombed-out terrain of their West Berlin and wonders if, despite the penurious conditions, it was easier to make art then Feral musicians emerging from the rubble of bombed-out West Berlin (as composer György Ligeti described it, "a surrealist cage in which all those inside are free") and creating themselves out of their own blood and guts very much feels like a tale from another age. In a world of coffee shop startups, utilitarian computer software and ersatz bedroom electronica as aural wallpaper, building your own percussive instruments from scrap might seem primitive, complex, redundant even. But in 1981, when Einstürzende Neubauten made Kollaps, it was revolutionary. For the briefest... The post Concrète Dschungel: Einstürzende Neubauten’s Kollaps At 45 appeared first on The Quietus.
items._genre: industrial / experimental / noise / post-punk
items._cn_summary: 这张1981年的首张专辑以废料自制打击乐器为核心手段，金属撞击、电钻、钢板等工业噪音被组织成节奏结构，彻底突破了传统乐器与音色的边界。乐评追溯了乐队在西柏林废墟中诞生的创作语境，将其与利盖蒂形容的"超现实主义牢笼"相联系——物质匮乏反而催生了极端的物质美学。专辑用噪音作为材料而非装饰，探讨了后工业城市中声音与空间的关系，混凝土丛林既是物理环境，也是声音隐喻。尽管文章为节选片段，未能深入分析具体曲目的结构与声音层次，但其历史定位与艺术理念已被清晰勾勒，对于理解欧洲工业与实验音乐的源头具有参考价值。

items.body: Review by DimitrisTheHead — Truly mind blowing album. Arguably one of the most manifold records from the dusk of that decade. HIGH TIDE have been one of the most important underground rock acts of that era. This album really blew my mind the first time I heard it. I almost did not believe that it released in 1969. Very few bands were so heavy back then. HIGH TIDE is so damn heavy, it really pisses me off that I can't recall a single magazine or online "list" of proto-metal bands that mentions these guys. You can find fragments of early doom in songs like "Futilist's lament" & "Missing out". You can hear neoclassical influences on the guitar riff on "Walking down their outlook". Also, on the same song, listen carefully the guitar lick on 2:20 (Judas Priest anyone?!?!?). And that violin... Majestic. Enchanting. Listen to "Pushed, but not forgotten". Amazing stuff, honestly. Some people may say that the [&*!#]ty production fits with the music and the atmosphere, I say it steals the music's grandeur.
items._genre: heavy prog / psychedelic rock / proto-metal
items._cn_summary: 这张1969年的专辑是英国地下摇滚场景中常被忽视的重量级作品，将迷幻、前卫与重金属的雏形融为一体。乐队以小提琴作为核心乐器之一，营造出既壮丽又迷幻的声响质感，区别于同时代多数硬摇滚乐队依赖吉他的传统配置。评论指出作品已显现早期doom的片段特征，吉他部分受新古典主义影响，某些riff甚至预示了后来Judas Priest的发展方向。小提琴与失真吉他的交织创造出独特的紧张感与史诗感，但评论者也批评其粗糙的制作削弱了音乐本应具备的宏大气势。作为早期前卫摇滚与重金属交叉点的稀有录音，它对研究地下摇滚史与proto-metal起源具有重要价值，但其粗粝的制作风格和1969年的时代局限也使得整体完成度有所欠缺。

items.body: Review by memowakeman — Review originally posted at www.therocktologist.comA third exquisite offering. The talented Italian quartet Aether is back with an incredibly solid, mature, refined, and creative album, one that fans of jazz fusion, progressive rock, and music that appeals to the senses will enjoy from beginning to end. Across 43 minutes and six tracks, the musicians treat us to a series of sonic landscapes that range from relaxing to frenetic, from atmospheric to deeply sensory, moving seamlessly between rock, post-rock, ambient, and classical music. It all begins with "Oort Cloud," whose opening seconds are atmospheric and otherworldly, creating a contemplative, dark mood. Little by little, new elements and sounds emerge, making you feel as though you are floating through space, caught somewhere between uncertainty and curiosity, until everything erupts at the 2:30 mark and a new rhythm takes over, retaining that dark sound that at times reminds me of early-70s King Crimson. As the minutes go by, the band introduces more colors, with the keyboards becoming a crucial element. Nevertheless, the atmospheres created by the bass, guitar, and drums come together to form a truly fascinating sonic experience. Next comes "Vogon," where the bass maintains a steady pulse while the guitar, keyboards, and drums appear here and there, gradually moving from uncertainty toward a sense of resolution as a distinctly jazzy melody begins to take shape. The very distinctive voice of the theatrical Claudio Milano emerges to recite a poem, creating one of the album's most unique moments. Shortly after his voice fades away, the music explodes, and jazz gives way to rock, with Andrea Ferrari's guitar charging forward like a whirlwind of emotions, compelling you to move and simply enjoy the music. The sonic landscapes shift in fascinating ways on "Cinq Teintes, Quatre Cadres." It begins by creating spacious, otherworldly soundscapes that, after two and a half minutes, take on an almost psychedelic essence, thanks first to the hypnotic bass of Andrea Grumelli, who guides the way as the guitar, synths, and drums deliver a daring and wonderful blend of space rock and jazz. This is one of my favorite tracks on the album. "La M�lancolie Du Petit Prince" features Andrea Serino's piano as the central element and guiding force of this literary-inspired passage. Beyond the blend of jazz and classical music brought to life by the piano, I love the fretless bass and its wonderfully fluid, graceful notes. I am also particularly fond of the deliciously sensory percussion Matteo Ravelli plays at the beginning, which he later contrasts with his electronic devices. Another majestic moment arrives with "Panta Rei." Its eight minutes unleash the quartet's imagination and creativity, showing us that after three studio albums, these musicians understand one another exceptionally well and flow together naturally, not only as accomplished instrumentalists but, more importantly, as a band. And although there are several darker, denser moments, I love the balance they achieve, as we suddenly find ourselves immersed in passages that feel bright and full of promise. At one point, they even reminded me of Focus. And yes, progressive rock is very much present here. Finally, the album reaches its brilliant conclusion with "Swerve." Over the course of its ten minutes, Aether delivers the climax of the entire work, a clear testament to the evolution of their sound and their boundless creativity. The band brings together a rich mix of genres and emotions, allowing listeners to immerse themselves in progressive passages, profound atmospheres, and enveloping, emotionally charged textures. The rhythm and intensity gradually build from the halfway point onward, creating a sonic spectrum that makes you want to move with the music, feel it, savor every moment, and truly make it your own. Congratulations to Aether on such a solid release. I absolutely loved it.
items._genre: post-rock / jazz fusion / progressive rock / ambient
items._cn_summary: 意大利四人乐队Aether第三张专辑延续其跨类型探索路线，六首曲目在四十三分钟内构建出从氛围到激烈的声景。作品以'Oort Cloud'开场，氛围段落逐渐爆发，键盘在色彩铺陈中占据关键位置，贝斯、吉他与鼓的层次构建出具有空间感的声响体验。'Vogon'引入Claudio Milano的剧场化念白，随后爵士旋律过渡为吉他主导的摇滚段落。'Cinq Teintes, Quatre Cadres'在迷幻与太空摇滚之间游走，催眠式贝斯线牵引整体结构。'La Mélancolie Du Petit Prince'以钢琴为核心，融合爵士与古典元素，无品贝斯的流畅线条与电子打击器形成对比。'Panta Rei'长达八分钟，展现乐队三位成员间的自然流动与成熟的器乐默契。整张专辑在摇滚、后摇滚、氛围与古典之间无缝切换，融合度与想象力均有所体现。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — When I first heard a few tracks by this Finnish band, I gradually realized that what captivated me was the blend of King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard's irreverence toward musical genres, an approach that, while experimenting with them all, still respects them and follows their rules. I was also reminded of The Cardigans: a mix of tradition and the past, combined with a freshness where technology, jazz, and a unique brand of pop came together. Their debut album opens on a serious note with classical piano and violins, key elements of their sound, and the magical voice of Eeva Rajakangas; on the track "T�nne saakka ei aurinko paista," she recites the lyrics, creating a powerful and truly special moment. Kadenssi reveals the strong influence of Nordic traditional music, austere, profound, and almost sacred, and Celtic music, danceable and luminous, sharing a common thread in that both border on the mystical.With the fourth track, Kahdeksas p�iv�, rock and modernity enter the mix, while maintaining that distinctive nine-piece lineup, featuring two violins and a saxophone, where the true fusion begins. A folk atmosphere, driven by the flute, occasionally evokes the folk-rock sound of Jethro Tull; yet, modern drum loops and Eeva's spoken-word vocals merge into a blend of jazz, funk, and punk. Add to this a dissonant chorus and a distorted, psychedelic cabaret vibe, and it feels as though we are witnessing a whole new album within the album itself."Planeetta" plays with space and silence; Eeva's voice sings and then recedes, as does the piano, eventually revealing a jazz-infused atmosphere driven by violins and saxophone, lending the track a distinctive character. It then returns to Celtic roots, yet approaches them not in the traditional manner, but with a rock and funk sensibility, featuring a syncopated, irregular rhythm."08" continues with the distinctly postmodern vibe created by Eeva's spoken vocals, almost prophetic in tone, which has become a signature, recognizable style for the band. Just as Pessi Jouste's classical training is evident in the violin work, Aino Kallio's influence shines through on the piano; at times, the music evokes the atmosphere of chamber music, at others, Eastern and jazz styles reminiscent of Hiromi Uehara, or even the experimental approach of Alain Rochette (from the band Present). When the sound grows heavier, it becomes dense and dark, yet the strings and Eeva Rajakangas are always there, ensuring we never quite plunge over the precipice."Tarina" ventures into new territory; while Eeva sings and phrases with great freedom, she does so in tandem with a band that evokes the anarchic melodies of the Lounge Lizards, until the violins launch into a sort of tango reminiscent of the track "Palmiers En Pots" by the Belgian group Aksak Maboul. It is not even far-fetched to draw parallels with the Rock in Opposition scene; one can even detect traces of the early, defiant Bj�rk, alongside the bass-clarinet blues of Jaakko Arola."Vesi" evokes a violin-infused cabaret sung by Ute Lemper, yet the arrangements steer the sound toward danceable rhythms infused with punk currents, waves that surge in and recede. The band adapts perfectly to this variety of styles, skillfully navigating the challenge of maintaining overall cohesion. They stand as an impenetrable, unbreakable shield, much like the Baltic Shield, reflecting that Nordic light which lasts for months; a duration that pales in comparison to the enduring scope of their musical and artistic vision.

items._cn_summary: 芬兰九人乐队VIMMA的首张专辑在北欧传统民谣与凯尔特音乐的基础上进行了大胆的跨界实验。钢琴与小提琴构成核心音响骨架，萨克斯与长笛的加入使作品呈现出室内乐般的精致质感。Eeva Rajakangas的人声时而演唱、时而念白，甚至带有预言般的宣叙调色彩，成为乐队最具辨识度的签名。专辑融合了爵士、放克、朋克、迷幻cabaret等元素，电子鼓循环与失真人声打破了民谣的抒情框架。挪威、凯尔特、东欧乃至东方音乐的影响交织其中，对话Björk、Lounge Lizards、Aksak Maboul等乐队的实验气质。整张作品在严肃古典气质与反叛精神之间游走，既保持对各流派的尊重，又不拘泥于任何既定规则。

items._cn_summary: 华沙之秋音乐节是当代音乐领域最具野心的盛会之一，以其庞大的策划规模与多元的曲目编排著称。今年开幕周末的周日几乎被两场大型演出所占据，展现了节日一贯的高强度策展理念。音乐节涵盖当代古典与现代作曲的核心范畴，同时广泛吸纳先锋与实验音乐的边界探索，演出形式涵盖独奏、室内乐以及大型合奏等多种编制。对于关注二十世纪与二十一世纪新音乐动态的听众而言，华沙之秋提供的是一个集中聆听前沿作品、与作曲家及演奏家直接对话的场域，也是欧洲当代音乐生态的重要风向标。

Jeremy Cunningham
items.body: Label: Northern Spy Records, 2026 Personnel - Jeremy Cunningham: drumset, percussion, piano, Rhodes, organ, vibes, electronics; Jeff Parker: guitar; Josh Johnson: alto saxophone, electronics; Dustin Laurenzi: guitar, synth, programming, tenor saxophone; Matt Gold: guitar, bass, pandeiro; Greg Uhlmann; guitar, electronics; Will Miller: Rhodes, electronics; Sen Morimoto: vocals; Lia Kohl; cello; Paul Bryan: bass, electronics; Lane Beckstrom: bass; Makaya McCraven: drumset, vibes. Jeremy Cunningham is an alert and versatile multi-instrumentalist based in Chicago since 2009. I was very well impressed with his previous outing, A Better Ghost (2022), featuring a few members who reappear on Passing Fires , namely saxophonists Dustin Laurenzi and Josh Johnson, bassist Paul Bryan, and trumpeter-turned-keyboardist Will Miller. Other illustrious guests here include guitarists Jeff Parker and Matt Gold, and sophisticated drummer Makaya McCraven. Instead of fixed formats, Cunningham favors a rotation of musicians who have an ear for careful sonic detail. The album has a very personal feel to it, evolving as a meditation on love, loss, memory, and change. Two of the strongest pieces are " To The Sky " and " Kobi Shobi ". While the former holds a wonderful collective bossa groove, featuring the multi-faceted Matt Gold on guitar, bass, and pandeiro, Cunningham on Rhodes, McCraven's soulful drumming, and Japanese-American Sen Morimoto's ethereal, wordless vocal work, the latter is unexpectedly edgy, bolstered by funk throbs and a jazzy hip-hop vibe that takes us to A Tribe Called Quest and Digable Planets. Johnson's snaky alto solo boosts the energy over the syncopated guitar comping offered by Parker. Also filled with joy and aplomb, " Union Pier " is a compelling 3/4 duo piece that pairs Cunningham on drum set and percussion with Laurenzi, who, besides tenor—on which he offers a fluid improvisation—also injects guitar, synth, and percussion. " Beyond the Veil " is a 4/4 pop/rock piece with rounded harmonic contours and a graceful melody, featuring McCraven on vibes, and Parker, who claims the spotlight while injecting deep feeling into his impromptu statement. He also appears on the pop-meets-R&B " Some Days ”. Bryan's six-beat funky groove stretches into asymmetry and a different figure on " Galloway Street ", which welcomes guitarist Greg Uhlmann and shines a spotlight on Johnson's effect-drenched alto solo. The album closes in a Sade-like sophisti-pop style with " Somewhere To Be ", featuring Morimoto's smooth styling. Cunningham's compositions have a strong emotional arc, and that quality rings true in the music. Melding jazz-imbued improvisation into different stylistic frameworks, Passing Fires works as an escape from traditional jazz moves. Favorite Tracks: 03 - To The Sky ► 06 - Kobi Shobi ► 10 - Galloway Street

items._cn_summary: 专辑由芝加哥鼓手兼多乐器演奏家Jeremy Cunningham领衔，汇集多位客座乐手，采用灵活的轮换编制而非固定乐队形式。作品围绕爱、失去、记忆与变迁展开，情感弧线清晰。Cunningham本人演奏鼓、钢琴、Rhodes电风琴、管风琴、颤音琴及电子设备，跨越多种声学与电子音色。专辑融合爵士即兴与多种风格框架：bossa nova律动、funk律动、Sade式的sophisti-pop、流行摇滚、hip-hop氛围等，部分曲目带有Tribe Called Quest和Digable Planets式的爵士嘻哈质感。Jeff Parker、Josh Johnson、Dustin Laurenzi等客座乐手贡献了富于变化的吉他与萨克斯线条，Matt Gold一人承担吉他、贝斯与pandeiro多种角色，Makaya McCraven在鼓与颤音琴间切换。整体作为对传统爵士语汇的逃离之作，在风格多样性与情感表达上具有较强的个人印记。
