items.body: …O sun, that healest all distempered vision, thou dost content me so, when thou resolvest,that doubting pleases me no less than knowing! -Dante Alighieri, Divine Comedy Golden Apes have spent more than twenty years making music for people who think a bass guitar should sound slightly dangerous, a baritone ought to carry bad news with dignity, and every decent chorus deserves at least one guitar line large enough to knock over the furniture. On The Sun Came Up Tremendously, the Berlin band sounds completely at home with that assignment. Ten songs move between post-punk, dark wave, gothic rock, dreampop, and bruised alternative rock, yet the record never feels like a display cabinet of influences. Golden Apes know this country too well for tourism. They have lived here. There is plenty of history in these songs, of course. You can hear The Cure in the open space around certain guitar lines, Chameleons in the upward sweep of others, Cocteau Twins in the gauzier passages, and the severe romantic machinery of Clan of Xymox when the keyboards begin closing in. White Lies, Interpol, Lowlife, and The Horrors, drift through the bloodline. Yet Golden Apes have reached the point where influence is less a matter of borrowing than instinct. Twenty-plus years will do that to a band. Eventually your record collection gets absorbed into your nervous system. The Sun Came Up Tremendously follows 2024’s Our Ashes at the End of the Day as the second installment in a planned trilogy, with material written across 2024 and 2025 and recorded at Thommy Hein Studios in Berlin between late 2025 and early 2026. Thommy Hein also contributes guitar, joining vocalist and keyboardist Peer Lebrecht, guitarists Maximilian Hennig and Stephan Schoenfeld, bassist Christian Lebrecht, and drummer Salomon Bosse. The production favors size without polishing away the pressure inside these songs. Basslines keep pushing forward, drums give the record a stern physical gait, and the guitars are allowed to bloom, bruise, and occasionally swallow the room. Farewell begins with a plaintive guitar that sounds as if it’s emerging from a dream, and an open space that immediately calls The Chameleons to mind, though The Horrors’ later grandeur also shows in the way the arrangement keeps adding height. It is a lovely opening, sad without collapsing into self-pity, and expansive without turning into marble-statue rock. Peer Lebrecht sings as though he has already accepted whatever the song is grieving, which somehow makes the ache sharper. By the time the rhythm section settles in, the track feels less like a goodbye than the long walk away from one. The Light (Inside Us) comes on harder. The guitars widen, Christian Lebrecht’s bass digs in, and the verses carry a conversational quality before the chorus breaks open into a shoegaze-heavy rush. The seduction of scale takes center stage: the chorus is huge enough to make a ceiling seem temporarily optional, yet the band keeps enough dirt in the guitars to prevent grandeur from becoming ceremony. This is music reaching for the upper rows while keeping both boots on the club floor. Milk and Poison turns inward and drops the temperature. Its opening feels like ripples on water with dream-pop textures, though the song soon settles into an anthemic ballad buoyed by these currents, sailing on broad synth pads, acoustic accents, surging guitars, and Peer’s low, expressive voice. He has one of those voices that can make a grocery list sound vaguely incriminating, and Golden Apes wisely avoid burying it beneath unnecessary decoration. The arrangement gives him room, then closes around him in slow degrees. Resistance is where the record’s architecture comes into sharpest focus. A resonant guitar figure opens the track, answered by a low keyboard tone, as hi-hats hiss at the edges and the bass builds steady pressure. The arrangement grows heavier until the guitars reach the emotional scale of mid-eighties gothic rock. Peer remains composed as the band swells around him, and that restraint gives the song its authority. Near the center, a clean, melodic guitar solo arrives with almost startling simplicity, offering a brief clearing before the vocal returns with greater weight. No pyrotechnics are needed; the song already knows where its gravity lies. At intervals, the drums break into splashes and the rhythm pulls back, leaving more air around Peer’s euphoric delivery. The measured bass, sober guitar tone, and baritone gravity recall Scottish cult band Lowlife, while the surrounding textures remain recognizably Golden Apes. Helion heads toward the same terrain as Clan of Xymox and The Chameleons, with traces of Joy Division in its resigned vocals and the stern drive of its rhythm section. An emotional barrage of drums and surging guitars carries the song forward, giving its sense of exhaustion an almost overwhelming physical force. There is something perversely satisfying about how controlled it remains amid all that turbulence. Plenty of bands mistake gloom for permission to wallow; Golden Apes keep pushing through it. It is the sort of song you want to hear live, feel in your chest, and carry with you on the walk home after everybody else has disappeared. Where the River Ran slows the pace and brings Peer’s baritone into Nick Cave territory. The drums begin with a plodding military tattoo, giving the song a processional character, while guitar and synth gradually stretch outward until the arrangement takes on a shoegaze breadth. The transition works because the band allows it to happen patiently. What begins in discipline ends in something far less contained. Evelyn (One Day) opens with a long sigh, which is about as efficient a piece of scene-setting as anybody could ask for. The resemblance to Lowlife grows even stronger here, recalling the Scottish band at their most wistful, thoughtful, and romantic. Dream-pop synth textures surround Peer’s voice, while dramatic splashes of guitar and percussion accent the song’s tender emotion, not unlike The Cure’s “Push.” Once again, Golden Apes take the form of a ballad and keep expanding it until the walls seem to move outward. The song swells like the ocean, its quieter passages gathering strength before euphoric surges of guitar and drums break across the arrangement. Their fondness for large choruses could become ridiculous in less experienced hands, but the rhythm section keeps the drama tethered to muscle. Radiation opens with a steady drumbeat and dirgeful tones before Peer’s rich, deep baritone bellows with unusual force, almost thunderous without losing definition. The chiming guitars and rhythm section pull back to give him room, though the melodic bassline remains palpable, felt in the heart and bones. With the song’s titular refrain, a surge of guitars seems to radiate toward the fingertips, giving its emotional release a physical reach. The drums then quicken in anticipation, and the guitars sweep in sustained arcs before the refrain returns, each repetition gathering strength from the space the band leaves around the voice. City Walls slows everything again, returning to the Cave-like gravity heard earlier. The drums drag with deliberate weight while a manic hi-hat keeps scratching at the surface, and eerie female backing vocals add an uneasy human presence around Peer’s lead. The song feels boxed in by design. Space exists, but none of it seems comfortable. Every instrument appears to occupy its own corner while the room keeps shrinking. Then comes Dreams (Gone By), opening with strange industrial textures before a weighty rhythm section and eerie synth tones take control, recalling London After Midnight’s Kiss. The percussion has real physical heft, but the gloom gradually recedes as the song opens into the brighter dream-pop romance of Modern English and Lowlife. Golden Apes carry that change with the emotional swell established throughout the album, letting the arrangement expand without losing the force of its darker beginnings. A brief pause for a wistful guitar chime offers some breathing room before the gothic dance rhythm returns, subtly brighter now, and the song surges again. As a closer, it gives the album one last change in texture, moving from industrial unease toward romantic release while retaining the emotional weight of the previous nine tracks. By this point, the record has passed through goth, post-punk, dreampop, dark wave, and broad alternative rock without sounding indecisive. Golden Apes can write a severe club track, a huge guitar chorus, a graveyard ballad, or a slow piece that sounds built for stained glass and bad decisions, and somehow Peer Lebrecht’s voice keeps the record unified. His baritone carries longing, isolation, regret, and the occasional flash of release without turning every lyric into a public execution. There is drama here, plenty of it, but the band understands proportion. Even at their biggest, they leave enough space for the songs to breathe. The Sun Came Up Tremendously is also the work of a band with very little interest in pretending they discovered any of these styles yesterday. Golden Apes’ long touring history, including appearances at Wave-Gotik-Treffen, Castle Party, and Murder of Crows, plus stages shared with The Chameleons, Pink Turns Blue, And Also the Trees, She Past Away, Whispering Sons, TRAITRS, Then Comes Silence, and others, has given them the practical education that comes from watching songs survive outside the studio. The title may promise sunrise, though nobody should expect birds chirping outside a kitchen window. Golden Apes prefer their light complicated, filtered through regret, desire, bad choices, and the stubborn suspicion that survival can occasionally be worth the inconvenience of a journey through hell and back. The only way to reach dawn, after all, is through the night. The Sun Came Up Tremendously is out now through Icy Cold Records. Listen to the album below and order here. items._cn_summary: Golden Apes 来自柏林，是一支成立超过二十年的暗潮后朋克乐队。这张专辑是他们计划中三部曲的第二部，延续了2024年作品的气质。乐队在十首歌中穿梭于后朋克、暗潮、哥特摇滚、梦幻流行与另类摇滚之间，但并非简单罗列风格标签，而是将The Cure、Chameleons、Cocteau Twins、Clan of Xymox等前辈的影响内化为本能。制作上追求宏大体积却不磨去歌曲内部的张力：贝斯线持续推进，鼓点赋予专辑庄严的步伐感，吉他则时而绽放时而吞噬空间。歌词引用但丁《神曲》开篇，以悲伤却不自溺的姿态展开，主唱Peer Lebrecht的男中音仿佛早已接受歌曲所哀悼之物，使痛感更加锐利。从开篇的梦境式吉他到后续硬朗的混响浪潮，专辑在克制与铺张之间找到了平衡。

items.body: Label: Out Of Your Head Records, 2026 Personnel - David Léon: saxophone, flute; Kenny Warren: trumpet; Stephan Crump: bass; Ches Smith: drums. Bassist and composer Stephan Crump, a musician of extraordinary passion and lyricism, put together a crisp, bright new ensemble for his latest outing, Passerine , a work of originals inspired by the various nesting techniques of birds. Relying on a frontline composed of Cuban-American saxophonist and flutist David Léon and trumpeter Kenny Warren, and pairing up beautifully with the resourceful drummer Ches Smith, Crump has something fresh to say. " Stuck " firstly evolves in a 3/4 time signature, displaying a big, round bass sound that shelters sharp unison melody. Léon narrates a story over an arco bass ostinato, while Smith explores toms and cymbal sounds with sagacity. There's a change of pace and texture for Warren's expressive solo, and the interplay between the rhythm team becomes more defiant, leading to a swinging passage before returning to the initial waltzing breeze. " Glide " is executed with a compelling rhythmic quality underneath—Crump incorporating effortless bass pedals, pizzicato routes, and cool grooves that find consistent support in Smith's nicely brushed skins. On flute, Léon stands out, drawing from melodic and harmonic minor modes in his improvisation. " Weavers " and " Twenty-Five " are warm meditative exercises where all members leave flowery scents in the air while rowing in the same direction. The former piece rests on a relaxed bass harmonic conduction that breathes at a challenging tempo, having charismatic, pure-toned unisons running atop. The latter is a shape-shifter that initiates with a sparse bass figure, understated drumming, a pellucid flute whose gentle dance emulates the chirp of birds, and introspective trumpet. Warren and Léon always take maximum advantage of their instruments to create dual melodic lines that feel luminous and often varied in shape. That's the case on " Fly ", a well-balanced 3/4 canvas painted with a certain wry melancholia. Breathable bass and brush work create space and smooth out the environment, culminating in a pulsating bass pedal point at the center of the outro vamp. With sensitive collaborative input from the musicians enlisted, Passerine is a point of departure and an embrace of transformation for Crump. It's also detailed with rigor without abandoning the freedom of creating spontaneously. The composer's sophisticated sound and gracious storytelling are filtered into the album's sequence. Favorite Tracks: 01 - Stuck ► 02 - Glide ► 03 - Weavers

items._cn_summary: 贝斯手兼作曲家 Stephan Crump 以鸟类筑巢行为为灵感，邀请古巴裔美籍萨克斯/长笛手 David Léon、小号手 Kenny Warren 与鼓手 Ches Smith 组成全新四重奏。专辑围绕原创曲目展开，乐评详细剖析了《Stuck》《Glide》《Weavers》《Twenty-Five》《Fly》五首作品的织体与结构：3/4 拍华尔兹律动、弓弦低音持续音、长笛与弱音鼓刷营造的冥想氛围、双旋律线的层叠对话。整体演奏在严谨作曲框架下保留自发即兴空间，旋律温暖而克制，音色明亮通透，节奏部门在弓弦与拨弦之间频繁切换。对偏好现代爵士、即兴与学院派路线的听众而言是一次精致的室内爵士体验，但在前卫实验性、声响解构或跨界融合维度上相对保守，尚未突破传统爵士器乐框架。

items.body: Watch an exclusive premiere of the film of Ava Rasti’s The River, first performed as part of the 2025 Semibreve festival. The River by Iranian-born Berlin-based composer Ava Rasti was commissioned by Portuguese festival Semibreve and first presented on 25 October 2025 at the Capela Imaculada do Seminário Menor in Braga. The performance brought together Rasti and a string quartet composed of Filipa Abreu (violin), Vânia Oliveira (viola), Tiago Mendes (cello) and Catarina Coelho (cello). The work takes the Piave river in northern Italy as its inspiration, a landscape in which the present is intertwined with the traces of wars and violence from its past. Rasti constructs these fragmented memories, recontextualised and transformed into sounds. Wire subscribers can read Claire Sawer's review of Semibreve 2025 here.

items._cn_summary: 伊朗裔柏林作曲家Ava Rasti的委约作品《The River》以意大利北部皮亚韦河为灵感，这片土地上当代与战争创伤交织。作品将支离破碎的历史记忆重新语境化并转化为声响，由四名弦乐演奏者组成的弦乐四重奏呈现，2025年10月在葡萄牙布拉加首演。作品聚焦声音的记忆建构与时间层叠，属于当代古典写作框架内的实验性探索。原文为The Wire杂志的电影首映公告与作品背景介绍，并非完整乐评，信息量有限。

items.body: Anyankofo means friends in Fante, and the Danish seven-piece Total Hip Replacement have been collecting them in Ghana since a mini-tour there in 2013. In the winter of 2021 they formed a nine-piece band in Accra with Ghanaian highlife, reggae and gospel musicians and gave it that name, which also titles the album the group recorded at Kwame Yeboah‘s Kwashibu studio, released in 2022. A later trip to Ghana took them to Kumasi, the Ashanti capital and one of highlife’s strongholds, and a week of jamming there with players from Frafra gospel singer Florence Adooni‘s band and with Nsoroma of Accra highlife band Santrofi produced “The Search”. It is the latest single ahead of the album Ehum, and the band say it holds on to the improvised feel of the jams. The song is about hunting for purpose in a society that keeps speeding up, where the pressure to get ahead alone costs people their connection to each other. Singer and trombonist Victor West Hosbond fronts the band’s horn section, the signature of their sound, and on this single it rides a highlife rhythm. The band describe the mood they chased as “the hopeful spot between melancholy and euphoria“. They filmed the video over a couple of days at an old farmhouse in France during this summer’s tour, with Nell Le Corre behind the camera. Ehum, which the band translate as storm, comes out on 27 November with Ivorian reggae singer Tiken Jah Fakoly among the guests. A West African run through Senegal, Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana opens the tour, then Danish dates follow from February into April, among them ALICE in Copenhagen on 26 February and Aarhus on 27 March. items.body: Review by DimitrisTheHead — One of my favorite albums of 1969 hands down. So many styles of music one can find here. Blues, psychedelia, jazz, classical, rock. All of them combined to provide a sample of proto-prog in the late 60s British scene. Songs like "Isadora", "Waterways", "Bathers", "Moth" are majestic. Geoff Nicholson delivers some really beautiful and heart-warming vocal harmonies. But, Dave Arbus steals the show here. With his electric violin and his flute, he blesses our ears with some enchanting melodies. This album really could be close to perfect, if it weren't for those free jazz/improvisations on the songs "Centaur woman" & "In the stable of the Sphinx" which in my opinion kind of mess up a little bit the whole atmosphere of the album.Nevertheless, this is a really strong album, that the fans of the early prog rock era should check out.
items._genre: eclectic prog / psychedelic rock / proto-progressive / jazz fusion
items._cn_summary: 1969年英国前卫摇滚场景中的实验性专辑，融合布鲁斯、迷幻、爵士、古典与摇滚等多种风格。Geoff Nicholson的人声和声温暖而饱满，而Dave Arbus的电小提琴与长笛演奏成为最大亮点，呈现出令人沉醉的旋律线条。然而，专辑中"Centaur woman"与"In the stable of the Sphinx"两首曲目的自由即兴段落被认为略显冗余，一定程度上破坏了整体氛围的一致性。作为融合多种风格的前卫摇滚原型作品，展现了六十年代末英国音乐场景对风格边界的探索。

items._cn_summary: 挪威小号手兼电子音乐家尼尔斯·佩特·莫尔沃尔推出新专辑《Be Quiet》，延续其标志性的近未来电子爵士美学。这张专辑源于他与全球多位艺术家合作的计划，并配套有同名纪录片。参与合作的包括英国电子音乐人阿尔瓦·诺托（Alva Noto）、日本电子艺术家三井郁（Imogen Heap、DJ UIE等亦有涉及），以及传奇摇滚乐队齐柏林飞艇的贝斯手约翰·保罗·琼斯（John Paul Jones），阵容横跨电子、实验与摇滚领域。专辑据称是对ECM时期经典曲目的再构建基础上发展而来，通过不同艺术家的碰撞探索声音的新边界。整体定位介于爵士解构与电子实验之间，跨界合作是其核心创作方式。

items.body:
After the OĽUN album I reviewed enthusiastically a while back, here’s the next project, again motivated and led by violinist/fiddler/composer Ján Kružliak Jr., continuing the rapprochement, indeed embrace, between Slovakia’s traditional music and its classical music. This time it reconnects the works of classical composers who were inspired by and drew on village musics with those traditional sources and styles.
Three ensembles are involved: the Spectrum Quartett led by Kru�liak with two violins, viola and cello; Nogaband, the traditional-style quartet of fiddles, contra (chording viola) and bass that’s led by fiddler and singer Michal Noga; and the female vocal group Ulijanky, plus guest singer Simona Hulejov�.
The majority of the tracks are interpretations of works by Slovak composer Eugen Suchon (1908-1993), with others from fellow-Slovaks Ilja Zeljenka (1932-2007) and Alexander Moyzes (1906-1984), and Hungarian B�la Bart�k (1881-1945) who did a lot of his very detailed collecting of folk music in Slovakia.
In each case the sources - musicians and locations in villages across Slovakia - are credited in the notes, and these arrangements and performances reconnect with the energy and traditional vocal sound of those sources.
In no way is this an orchestra-smoothed thing; this is gutsy, brilliantly played and sung music with all the spirit, skill and technique of traditional music, from players and singers who deeply understand and inhabit it. It’s a glorious piece of work, music to luxuriate in. There’s too much richness to begin to detail, but here’s a dip into a few moments to give the flavor. The tracks all have very long titles detailing their sources, so for brevity’s sake I’ll just give track numbers.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由小提琴家兼作曲家Ján Kružliak Jr.主导，汇聚三组音乐力量：弦乐四重奏Spectrum Quartett、传统民间小提琴乐队Nogaband以及女声合唱团Ulijanky，将斯洛伐克古典作曲家Suchoň、Zeljenka、Moyzes及Bartók作品中汲取自乡村音乐的灵感，重新与原始民间素材和演奏风格对接。每首曲目都标注了采样来源的村庄乐手和地点，使改编与表演扎根于民间声乐传统。这不是被管弦乐磨平的声音，而是充满胆识的演奏与歌唱，展现了对传统音乐的深刻理解和技术掌控，将学院派古典与乡土血脉重新缝合。

items.body:
Though this recording documents the work of thirteen of Belgium's most innovative ensembles, the real star is the Park Abbey located just outside Leuven and founded in 1129. Built and maintained for the purpose of quiet meditation, the abbey hosted the musicians who used the quiet surroundings to prepare and record their unique musical imaginings. The result is a mostly instrumental collection that mines the riches of Belgian folk and world music traditions, including Romani scales,
La Pump
rhythms, and accordion-based
bal-musette
flavors.
For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑记录了十三支比利时创新乐团在鲁汶郊外帕克修道院的录音作品。修道院的石质空间提供了天然混响，三年的制作周期让录音品质温润而有层次。音乐内容横跨多种传统：斯洛文尼亚裔小提琴家Rénélíus Bikár以泛欧罗姆历史为脉络；Charlotte Pelgen用尤克里里与班卓琴音色演绎Django Reinhardt式摇摆；黎巴嫩裔歌手Amber Haddad以乌德琴融合地中海与阿拉伯声响；Andries Boone的曼陀林与羽管键琴组合呈现近乎巴洛克的音色。另有手风琴二重奏、喉音演唱与匈牙利齐特琴等元素。尽管风格跨度广泛，共享的修道院灵感赋予专辑内在统一性，整体偏向沉思与平和的氛围。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑聚焦乌克兰东部被俄罗斯绑架的约两万儿童的议题，将传统民歌与新作融合，以乌克兰-加拿大歌手Marichka为核心，联合两国音乐人录制，以弓弦乐器、班杜拉琴、钢琴为主要配器。专辑包含全女性加拿大人声组合Daughters of Donbas的作品，其中一位来自马里乌波尔的16岁少女曾是受害者之一，后成功返回乌克兰。歌曲取材于传统仪式与民间传说，如'Foreign Land'改编自讲述少女被迫离家务工的古老歌曲，'Rusalka'则以斯拉夫民间传说中的水妖为意象，旋律融合自然精灵的仪式性传统。整体以人声为核心，歌词承载沉重的历史记忆与当代战争创伤，音乐语言扎根于乌克兰民间传统，同时具备跨国合作的当代特征。

I want to personally direct you to a remarkable piece of music titled "Two Views of a Prayer," composed and written by
David Dzubinski
as part of the
Prism Quartet
's new series of collaborations called
Unlocking Your Inner Composer
. If you have listened to my radio programs, you are probably familiar with the quartet's ground-breaking, genre-blurring music. If not, there's no better introduction than this.
Performed in November of 2025 at the Free Library of Philadelphia, they invited vocalist
Ursula Rucker
, percussionist
Tyshawn Sorey
, and violinist
Carlos Santiago
to collaborate on the arrangement and performance of Dzubinski's composition. It travels from raw to lyrical and back in the course of just under 4 minutes, with both finesse and energy. - Cliff Furnald, editor
Find Prism Quartet online.

items._cn_summary: David Dzubinski 创作的四分钟作品《Two Views of a Prayer》由普林斯姆四重奏联合打击乐手 Tyshawn Sorey、小提琴家 Carlos Santiago 以及人声表演者 Ursula Rucker 于2025年11月在费城自由图书馆首演。该作品属于四重奏策划的「释放你的内在作曲家」系列委约计划，强调作曲者与演奏家之间的协作过程本身。乐评指出，作品在不足四分钟内从粗粝即兴走向抒情歌唱再折返，乐句充满力度与细腻张力。文本提及Tyshawn Sorey的参与尤为值得关注——作为当代学院派自由爵士与新音乐领域的核心人物，他的加入暗示了这部作品跨越当代古典、即兴与说唱叙事的边界。整体而言，文章偏向推荐性质，实际音乐分析篇幅极短，更多是节目主持人的导赏引介。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 这是丹麦三人组合GuldGanger的首张数字EP，由北欧民谣圈资深主唱Mia Guldhammer领衔，共收录五首作品，以传统音乐为主调，仅一首为乐队成员原创。整体氛围古朴、略带粗粝质感，节奏与器乐编排展现出成熟的乐队默契。开场曲《Svennedal》以奔放节奏展示了主唱极具说服力的声线；《Nordgård》由Morten Musicus原创，口簧与风笛推动音乐前行；《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》以扬琴铺陈细腻背景；终曲《Orms》作为器乐曲，由口簧、笛与弦乐交织，营造出弹性而略带失衡的听觉体验。尽管篇幅有限，EP已展现出乐队成熟的音乐素养，让听众对其完整专辑充满期待。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / documentary / lo-fi
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑并非传统意义上的音乐作品，而是由录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区街头录制的枪支暴力幸存者口述实录。二十五位参与者年龄从十七岁到六十七岁不等，许多人是临时被吸引加入的。录制当天正值特朗普下令向该市部署国民警卫队，地点位于一位九十四岁祖母家的前廊，处于Midway机场降落航道下方。录音中混杂了街头环境声、邻里对话、freestyle说唱片段，没有任何后期添加的音乐。一位失去两个儿子的长者在分享过程中情绪崩溃，反复道歉，但编辑指出该道歉的应是社会而非受害者。项目收益将捐赠给Cure Violence Global。尽管不属传统音乐范畴，但作为声音田野记录与城市社会现实的听觉文献，它与实验录音、现场艺术等领域有交集。

items._cn_summary: 本周精选涵盖暗氛围、嗡鸣、电声音乐、自由即兴与实验电子五个方向，共推荐五张专辑：Ruptured World 的《Spacefold》与 Dirk Serries 的《Curves of Splendor》属于氛围与嗡鸣范畴，后者以吉他即兴著称；Torn / Rainey / Berne / Dunn 的《DISCO TENT/RAVENS LOW & READY 2》汇集四位自由即兴乐手，融合萨克斯、吉他与鼓的对话；Oïkoumen 的《Resilience》延续电声音乐路线；Satøri 的《Your Life Is Worth Nothing》则偏向实验电子表达。从标题与厂牌信息判断，五张作品均来自独立小众渠道，风格跨度较广，但原文仅为简短列表式推介，缺少具体的演奏技法、声响细节与制作背景描述，信息量有限，难以深入评估每张专辑的独特性与艺术价值。整体推荐方向与暗潮、实验电子、即兴音乐爱好者契合度较高。

items.body: Review by Andis — Here's a record that deserves a lot more love. We Never Lost Control is one of those albums Igenuinely enjoy, and every spin leaves me in a better mood than before. After all, what's the pointof music if it doesn't entertain you and put a smile on your face?This album will never be mentioned in the same breath as the undisputed giants of progressive rock,but that hardly matters. It's a record I keep coming back to, and one I enjoy tremendously. Germanoddballs Nine Days Wonder, a band that seemed determined to reinvent themselves with every release,followed up their wonderfully bizarre debut by making a complete stylistic U-turn. The result is analbum that's surprisingly difficult to pin down.If I had to try, I'd place it somewhere between David Bowie and Van der Graaf Generator, with atouch of Genesis and Nektar sprinkled on top. What they play could broadly be called progressiverock, but that's only part of the story. There's glam rock swagger, flashes of krautrock, bursts ofhard rock, hints of jazz rock, and all of it fronted by a wonderfully (!) theatrical vocalist. Inother words, this album stubbornly refuses to sit in a single genre box.The band's greatest strength is its energy. Driven by swirling organs and keyboards, backed by aheavy and aggressive bass, they charge through inventive progressive rock that somehow manages tocombine the punch of hard rock with the structure of prog and the occasional hook of melodic pop-rock. Had I not known they were German, I would have guessed they were British without hesitation.Side A is a thoroughly enjoyable affair, filled with melodic songs that contain just enoughprogressive trickery to keep things interesting. But it's on Side B that the real fun begins. Herethe band completely lets loose, delivering colorful, adventurous prog rock with the magnificentnine-minute epic "We Grasp the Naked Meat" as the undisputed centerpiece.We Never Lost Control is a lovable little gem of an album: quirky, energetic, unpretentious, andendlessly entertaining. Think of it as a bag of mixed candy for progressive rock fans. Maybe itisn't a masterpiece, but it's the sort of record that reminds you why digging through the lesser-known corners of the genre can be so rewarding.
items._genre: progressive rock / glam rock / krautrock / hard rock / jazz rock
items._cn_summary: NINE DAYS' WONDER 的第二张专辑在他们首张作品之后做了风格上的急转弯，将前卫摇滚与华丽摇滚、硬摇滚、爵士摇滚的元素混合在一起，难以归入单一类型。评论将这张作品置于Bowie与Van der Graaf Generator之间，并提到Genesis和Nektar的影响。专辑A面以旋律性较强的歌曲为主，穿插适度的前卫元素；B面更为大胆，以九分钟长曲为核心，展示了乐队更自由的创作状态。键盘与管风琴是主导乐器，低音厚实且有冲击力，演唱者风格戏剧化。评论未给出具体的历史或文化背景分析，但指出乐队听起来像是英国乐队而非德国乐队，乐评整体带有推荐性质但认为该作并非杰作，只是值得发掘的小众之作。

items.body: Review by yarstruly — This is from my blog "Scott's Song by Song Spotlights" with links for listening and purchasing.Clicked 5, but really a 4.5...4 is too low!T.A.P are a progressive rock band led by composer/keyboardist Michael Jobborn. On their first album, which I have not heard (2023's "Paradigms") the band was rounded out by Warr-guitarist/multi-instrumentalist Mark Cook (Phase of Twilight and others) and Guitarist/Vocalist/multi-instrumentalist Suzi James (Fearful Symmetry, whose wonderful latest album "I've Started?So I'll Finish" is reviewed on this blog as well!). Paul Sears and Bill Bachman were both contributors on the first album on the drum throne. This time around Bill Bachman is a full member. Bill is renowned for his work as a drumming educator, including his work with several Drum Corps around the US. (DCI- Drum Corps International- is a deep rabbit hole that I have been familiar with since my college days!) But his prog resume is impressive as well: (From the press release) "Bill is the drummer for Herd of Instinct, Spoke of Shadows, has toured with progressive rock artist Neal Morse, is on recordings with Trey Gunn (King Crimson), Colin Edwin (Porcupine Tree), Adam Holzman (Miles Davis & Steven Wilson), and Gerald Albright (Grammy award winning saxophonist)". So, the musical talent in this band is absolutely staggering!This album comes courtesy of Anne-Claire Rallo of Bad Dog Promotions. As always, I receive no additional compensation and am free to "call it like I hear it". In fact, when I received the email offering this review to me from Anne-Claire, I replied, "You had me at Suzi James". The album "Paradigms II" is to be released on October 3, 2026, on the Prog Rock Essentials label (Ordering info follows the review). As per my usual method, this is a cold listen.Time to dig into the music!T.A.P are:Michael Jobborn - concepts, keysMark Cook - Warr guitar, bass, 12-string guitar, synth, sitar, strings, choirSuzi James - acoustic/electric guitars, keys, flute, violinBill Bachman - drums, percussionAdditional Contributors on tracks:2. Chris Gill - guitarChris Messina - synth4. Steve Bonino - guitar, lyrics/vocals5. Gayle Ellett - mellotron, acoustic/electric guitars6. Massimo Pieretti - piano, synthGayle Ellett - bouzouki, mellotron8. Tenk van Dool - mandolin, guitarChris Gill - guitarTrack 1 - Galaxy Unknown (4:28)An organ riff, accented with drums starts us off with an odd meter. The rest of the band soon joins in. There is a guitar solo after around 45 seconds. A softer section follows with alternating acoustic and electric instruments in the spotlight. This is a wonderful instrumental musical journey with many layers. As one might expect, the talent level here is through the roof! A terrific opener!Track 2 - A Beacon of Light (12:17)This one fades in with some guitar effects and synth tones. It feels like the first rays of sunlight at dawn, matching the title. Electric piano chords bring a sense of rhythm. The bass line provides melodic movement. The chords are layered among many instruments, giving a rich tonal palate. This is moving at a moderately slow tempo and a relaxed feel. The guitar solo that happens at around the 4-minute mark brings a balance of melodicism and complexity. A droning section after that leads to an upbeat groove on the bass and drums. It begins to take on a jazz fusion flavor. Synth and guitar solos float over the top of the rhythm bed. Just before 7:30 things calm down and a new section begins. Sitar sounds are a part of the soundscape. Bill's marching band experience shows in his snare part. At 8:45 we are down to lead guitar, bass and keys. The drums subtly return. We are in a slower 6-8 at this point. At 9:55 a more strident beat that reminds me of old TV themes takes over. There are so many moods in this piece; I love it! At 11:30, it reminds me of how it began. What an absolutely fantastic instrumental piece of music!Track 3 - A Dramatic Interlude (4:06)Electric piano, bass and lead guitar start this off. The drums enter a moment later. This is in a moderately slow 6-8, so far, but the title tells me something is going to happen. The tempo increases slightly and becomes more rhythmic after a small crescendo. I believe that is the Warr guitar taking the solo that follows. I love the staccato bass and guitar riff at around 2:20. Things begin to build up at around 3:20. The track ends with a long, sustained chord. A wonderful piece, but not as dramatic as the title indicated. Track 4 - A Hole in the Ground (6:14)Rich electric piano chords and clean guitars start us off here. Lead guitar emerges. And then--Vocals! Guest musician Steve Bonino is on this track with guitars and vocals. (This is not the first time his name has appeared in one of my reviews!) The drums begin to emerge as we progress. Mark Cook's basslines are fantastic on this album. Steve's voice seems a little buried in the mix at times. The drums might be a little too far back at times, as well. I like the song, but I don't feel like it's mixed as well as it could be. It would benefit from a better presentation. It ends with droning sounds.Track 5 - 4th Dimensional Wave (11:50)Sound effects fade in and guitars join. This starts out sounding like some sort of alarm. Soon, though, the music gets melodic with a fantastic guitar solo; I believe it is Suzi James. We are in a moderately slow tempo. The keys are playing a mellotron style chorus behind the solo. Some intricate rhythmic patterns follow. This keeps building, slowly and gradually. At around 4:20 we get into odd meters. At 5:45, the rhythm shifts into a different groove. I am really enjoying this one! There are tons of changes! Gayle Ellet of Djam Karet and his band the Electromags adds his keyboard abilities to the soundscapes. Probably my favorite track, so far.Track 6 - Lyrical Paradox (3:50)This one has a bit of a swing to it. Sort of a mellow melodic tune. The sound gets bigger just after the one-minute mark. Great melodies in this one. I love the slide guitar in it; it reminds me of the slide guitar in "And You and I" from Yes. This is a nice little piece. Ellet is back with bouzouki on this, and Massimo Pieretti (whom I have reviewed as well) adds keyboards.Track 7 - Outlooks of the Closed-Minded (6:29)This opens with some accents and jazz chords. It has a fusion feel to my ears. I love the syncopated rhythms. It reminds me of the Dixie Dregs a bit. Lots of melodies wind their way through this one. Wonderful track!Track 8 - Wishful Solitude (:)This one is more up-tempo, yet lighthearted. As with most of the album, the melodies are abundant! At around 3:15 Suzi plays her flute. There are many interesting things in the soundscape. At just be for the 5-minute mark, a descending synth part that sounds like the 70s idea of a UFO landing takes over, then we get a bit funky! At around 6:45 we get a psychedelic organ sound. This is a very cool piece with many different things going on. Tenk van Dool (who I am not familiar with) plays the mandolin at around 8:45. The melodies intertwine as we approach the ending. This is a wonderfully arranged prog instrumental. Great way to end this wonderful album.OVERALL IMPRESSIONS:I really liked that a lot! Unfortunately, I am not sure what happened on track 4, "A Hole in the Ground". I have always liked Steve Bonino's contributions, and he always seems to be a good guy in the online interactions I have had with him, but something just didn't work for me on that track. Otherwise, this is a fantastic album of mainly instrumental prog with some fusion tendencies. I give this a 4.5 out of 5 or 90%. Recommended!
items._genre: eclectic progressive rock / prog rock
items._cn_summary: 这是一张以键盘为核心的前卫摇滚专辑，由作曲家Michael Jobborn领衔，集合了Warr吉他、多种乐器和经验丰富的鼓手阵容。乐队成员横跨多个前卫摇滚项目，额外贡献者带来了mellotron、布祖基琴、曼陀林等多种音色，丰富了音乐层次。专辑包含器乐曲和人声作品，结构上注重段落变换与器乐solo，融合了管风琴、电钢琴、合成器等键盘元素。原文章为逐曲乐评，详细描述了开篇曲目的奇数拍编排与多层次器乐铺陈，但内容因截断而未呈现完整分析。整体制作偏向传统前卫摇滚框架，未见明显跨界实验元素，与实验/电子/即兴等前沿方向距离较远，适合偏爱经典prog语汇的听众。

items.body: Review by kenethlevine — A crisp, violin and guitar led prog act can't help but invoke a certain era of a certain UK prog monarch led by ROBERT FRIPP, and this instrumental album isn't unworthy of such a parallel, but this is mostly in the distorted icy leads and the jazz inflections. With no vocals and a tendency to prefer structured jamming over improv, not to mention a folk orientation that Crimson increasingly set aside after 1972, it would be as unfair to SCARLET THREAD as it is to an obvious mentor to stretch this analogy any further. A better comparison might be Montreal's TALISMA or, originating in the HACKETT school, MR GIL/BELIEVE or HARNAKIS. Among fellow Finns, perhaps AQUAPLAN but without vocals, at least for now.As I said, this is jamming but in a disciplined and repetitive way that generally works well enough and is nothing if not appealing to prog ears, though everything seems a bit interchangeable - throw in a guitar motif, enhance with violin, maybe add flute, then move on to another violin theme, and enhance with guitar, maybe add flute, and so on. Luckily these are all well orchestrated. The opener and closer seem to hit highest on the sustainability index, along with "Siipirikon Lento" (flight of the bird with the injured wing). More would emerge in the subsequent decade, with a few dramatic changes, so this is not one of those debuts that unwittingly doubled as a swan song. Mildly recommended, but more enthusiastically for certain listener profiles.
items._genre: progressive folk / psychedelic folk / instrumental prog
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以小提琴与吉他为核心乐器，构建了一部纯器乐的前卫民谣作品。编曲手法倾向于有结构的即兴段落而非自由即兴，整体在重复与变奏中推进，段落间乐器的交替搭配（小提琴、吉他、长笛）成为主要展开方式。评论指出其在爵士化的失真吉他音色上与某些英式前卫经典有相似气质，但整体更接近芬兰本土器乐前卫民谣的传统。首尾曲及其中一首被特别提及为全作最具持续性吸引力的段落。作品编排扎实但段落之间存在一定程度的可互换感，乐评对其评价温和，推荐给特定偏好的听众。

items.album: 山﨑健太｜『映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇』

items.excerpt: 会期：2026/08/07〜2026/08/23 東京芸術劇場 シアターイースト［東京都］ 作・演出：岡田利規 公式サイト：https://www.geigeki.jp/performance/theater412/ 誰が舞台に立ち、誰が客席に座るのか。誰が誰を表象し、誰がそれを観るのか。『映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇』（作・演出：岡田利規）はそんな問いを改めて劇場へと持ち込み、そして観客に持ち帰らせるような作品だった。同作は岡田の東京芸術劇場舞台芸術部門芸術監督に就任第1作として上演されたもの。もともとはドイツのハノーファー州立劇場のレパートリーとして書かれ、5月に初演を迎えた岡田の現時点での最新作『Sliding Away』を、日本版の出演者・スタッフとともに新たに創り上げたものでもある。 タイトルが示す通り、舞台は映画を撮ろうとしているゾンビたちの撮影現場で展開する。登場するのは映画監督ゾンビのぽいぽい（東宮綾音）、俳優ゾンビのいいね（百瀬葉）、第5助監督ゾンビのまーしー（島田桃依）、第6助監督ゾンビのがーしー（石川朝日）、ゾンビ音楽家のげりま（福原冠）。しかし劇中で実際に映画の撮

誰が舞台に立ち、誰が客席に座るのか。誰が誰を表象し、誰がそれを観るのか。『映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇』（作・演出：岡田利規）はそんな問いを改めて劇場へと持ち込み、そして観客に持ち帰らせるような作品だった。同作は岡田の東京芸術劇場舞台芸術部門芸術監督に就任第1作として上演されたもの。もともとはドイツのハノーファー州立劇場のレパートリーとして書かれ、5月に初演を迎えた岡田の現時点での最新作『Sliding Away』を、日本版の出演者・スタッフとともに新たに創り上げたものでもある。 タイトルが示す通り、舞台は映画を撮ろうとしているゾンビたちの撮影現場で展開する。登場するのは映画監督ゾンビのぽいぽい（東宮綾音）、俳優ゾンビのいいね（百瀬葉）、第5助監督ゾンビのまーしー（島田桃依）、第6助監督ゾンビのがーしー（石川朝日）、ゾンビ音楽家のげりま（福原冠）。しかし劇中で実際に映画の撮影が行なわれることはない。ゾンビたちは現場に集まったはいいものの、主要な俳優もスタッフもやってこないため撮影をはじめられない状況にあるのだ。かくして、時間を持て余したゾンビたちはゾンビが映画を撮ることに関する持論を交わしはじめる。 『映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇』東京芸術劇場（2026年8月）［撮影：銀色なつみ］ 冒頭からいいねは、ゾンビが人間を演じるための人間メイクをするのには3時間45分もかかる一方、「人間がゾンビになるときのメイクはもっとずっと短時間でテキトーに済ませたってオッケーってされてるんだから」その非対称性には許しがたいものがあるとぶち上げる。あるいはぽいぽいは「どうしてわれわれゾンビがわれわれゾンビのこと考えるのに人間のつくったゾンビ映画参照しなきゃいけないのか」と言い、「人間のゾンビ表象からわれわれ自由になれる日がいつしかくるようにと願って」「ゾンビの視点で描くゾンビ映画」をつくろうとしているのだと宣言する。 『映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇』東京芸術劇場（2026年8月）［撮影：冨田了平］ 非対称性というキーワードからも明らかなように、ここではゾンビの存在が現実世界におけるさまざまなマイノリティと重ね合わせられている。劇中に登場するゾンビという言葉の大半は、そのまま例えばクィアという言葉に置き換えても──「クィアの視点で描くクィア映画」というようなかたちで──成立するだろう。言及される問題は多岐にわたる。例えばゾンビが登場する映画はすべてがゾンビ映画という括りに入れられてしまうということ。ゾンビは本当は人間と同じように歩くのであって「人間のゾンビ表象」は間違っているということ。残念ながらそんな「人間のゾンビ表象」によってゾンビが「教育」されてしまっている側面もあるということ。しかし「問題は人間の映画監督のゾンビ描写が貧しいってこと」ではなく「ゾンビの映画監督が圧倒的に少なすぎるっていうのが問題のほんとの所在」であるのだということ等々。 そして話題は観客のことにも及ぶ。ゾンビの観客はどれくらいいるのかと。しかもこの問いは、劇場にいる観客に向けて発せられるのだ。さらに舞台上のゾンビたちはおもむろにゾンビメイクを拭い去り、自分たちが「映画を撮りたいゾンビ」を演じる人間の俳優でしかないという身も蓋もない事実を観客に改めて突きつける。そうして明らかになるのは、舞台上にも客席にも、このゾンビについての演劇が上演されている劇場内にゾンビはひとりも存在していないという端的な事実だ。 『映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇』東京芸術劇場（2026年8月）［撮影：冨田了平］ 『映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇』東京芸術劇場（2026年8月）［撮影：相模友士郎］ ともすればポリコレ的言説の演説会にもなりかねない（というかそうでなかったとはなかなか言い切れない）この作品が、チャーミングな飽きさせない上演として成立していたのは俳優たちの魅力に負うところが大きいだろう。そのようなかたちで問いを社会へと持ち込めることもまた、演劇の可能性のひとつなのだ。 この『映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇』という作品は、『消しゴム山』（初演：2019）から『リビングルームのメタモルフォーシス』（初演：2023）へと展開する脱人間中心主義を掲げた岡田の一連の作品のひとつとしても位置づけられるだろう。そのコンセプトは『消しゴム山』では例えば「モノのための演劇」というきわめてラディカルなかたちで実現されていたが、同作では再演を重ねるなかで、アクセシビリティをめぐるさまざまな取り組みも実施されてきたのだった。それは中心とされてきたはずの人間のなかにも周縁化された存在がいるのだという、当然でありながら日本の演劇界においては十分に目が向けられてこなかった事実に改めて目を向ける取り組みでもある。ノン・ネイティブ日本語話者を出演者に迎えた『宇宙船イン・ビトゥイーン号の窓』（初演：2023）もこの系譜に連なる重要な作品だ。 劇場で配布されていた『劇場に置くノート1』に岡田は次のように記していた。「舞台芸術の上演が現状よりももっと、観客の身体やその振る舞いが肯定されている場になる。観客の身体どうしがその存在を肯定し合っているという場になる。そしたらそれはイノベーションだとおもう。どうやったらそれは起こせるだろう」。このような思想は岡田がアーティスティック・ディレクターを務める舞台芸術祭「秋の隕石」のプログラムや体制にも持ち込まれている。2026年の「秋の隕石」は10月9日（金）から11月3日（火）にかけての開催を予定している。 『映画を撮りたいゾンビの演劇』東京芸術劇場（2026年8月）［撮影：冨田了平］ 観賞日：2026/08/12（水） 関連記事 KYOTO EXPERIMENT 2023（前編） チェルフィッチュ『宇宙船イン・ビトゥイーン号の窓』｜高嶋慈：artscapeレビュー（2023年11月15日号） チェルフィッチュ×金氏徹平『消しゴム山』（エクストラ音声「山がつぶやいている」／配信版『消しゴム山は見ている』）｜山﨑健太：artscapeレビュー（2021年04月15日号） 没入するモノたち──チェルフィッチュ×金氏徹平『消しゴム山』｜池田剛介：フォーカス（2019年10月15日号）

items.body:
Stick Men are bringing their progressive rock explorations to Singapore.

The trio comprising Tony Levin, Pat Mastelotto, and Markus Reuter will perform at Singtel Waterfront Theatre on 29 January 2027 at 8PM. Presented by LAMC Presents, Tony Levin Stick Men – Live in Singapore will showcase the band’s unconventional instrumentation and intricate, rhythm-driven sound.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by L.A.M.C. (@lamcpresents)

Formed in 2007, Stick Men build their music around Levin’s Chapman Stick, Reuter’s 8-string Touch Guitar, and Mastelotto’s mix of acoustic and electronic percussion. Using two-handed tapping techniques, the string players weave together bass lines, melodies, and layered textures, giving the three-piece a sound that stretches well beyond a traditional rock trio.

Levin is best known for his longstanding work with King Crimson and Peter Gabriel, alongside recording and touring credits with artists including John Lennon, David Bowie, and Pink Floyd. Fellow King Crimson member Mastelotto, who co-founded Mr. Mister, brings loops, samples, and electronic textures into his drumming, while Reuter draws on a background spanning progressive rock, electronic music, and contemporary composition.

The Singapore date follows the September release of Let’s THRAK Again, the trio’s tribute to King Crimson’s 1995 album THRAK. Stick Men are touring the record across North and South America, Europe, and Asia, adding to a live history of more than 500 concerts in over 40 countries.

Tickets will be available via LAMC Presents, with sale details as follows:

LAMC members’ pre-sale: 7 October, 12PM SGT. Tickets priced at SGD98, SGD108, SGD118, and SGD128, with limited availability.

General sale: 8 October, 12PM SGT. Tickets priced at SGD98, SGD108, SGD128, and SGD138.

items.body: English post-punk band Killing Joke released their self-titled debut album, “Killing Joke,” on 5 October 1980 through E.G. Records, distributed by Polydor Records. The record turns 46 this year. Killing Joke recorded the album in August 1980 at Marquee Studios in London and produced it themselves, with Phil Harding as engineer. Drummer Paul Ferguson described the sessions as recorded live with “no overdubs to speak of.” The eight-track UK LP runs: “Requiem” “Wardance” “Tomorrow’s World” “Bloodsport” “The Wait” “Complications” “S.O.36” “Primitive” The original US pressing added “Change,” the B-side of the “Requiem” single, between “Complications” and “S.O.36.” “Wardance” came out as a single in February 1980, ahead of the album, and “Requiem” followed as a single in September 1980. The album entered the UK Albums Chart on 25 October 1980 at number 41 and later peaked at number 39. Its cover collages a photograph by Don McCullin of CS gas clashes in Derry, Northern Ireland, in 1971, designed by Mike Coles. In 2019, Pitchfork placed the album at number 9 on its list of the 33 best industrial albums of all time. “The Wait” was covered by Metallica on the 1987 “Garage Days Re-Revisited” EP and later included on “Garage Inc.,” “Primitive” was covered by Helmet in 1993, and “Requiem” was covered by Foo Fighters in 1997 as a B-side to “Everlong.” About Killing Joke Killing Joke formed in October 1978 in Notting Hill, London. Jaz Coleman (vocals, keyboards) and Paul Ferguson (drums) met in late 1978 and placed an announcement in Melody Maker in February 1979 reading “Bass, lead, to tell the killing joke, we mean it man!” Guitarist Geordie Walker and bassist Martin “Youth” Glover answered and completed the original line-up. The band released its debut EP, “Turn to Red,” as a 10-inch on 26 October 1979 on Malicious Damage, the label Killing Joke ran with graphic artist Mike Coles. Recorded in August 1979 at Gooseberry Sound in London, the EP drew airplay from BBC Radio 1’s John Peel. The “Almost Red” EP followed that November, and the single “Nervous System,” with “Turn to Red” as its B-side, came out in December 1979. Killing Joke then signed to E.G. Records for the self-titled debut album, released on 5 October 1980. The band’s next albums were “What’s THIS For…!” (1981) and “Revelations” (1982), after which Youth left the band and was replaced by Paul Raven on bass. “Fire Dances” followed in 1983 and “Night Time” in 1985, the album that carried the single “Love Like Blood” and brought the band its widest chart exposure to date. Killing Joke continued recording and touring into the 2010s with albums including “Absolute Dissent” (2010), “MMXII” (2012) and “Pylon” (2015), with Jaz Coleman and Geordie Walker as the group’s only constant members. Geordie Walker died in November 2023 at the age of 64, as Side-Line reported at the time. The band’s 1980 debut album remains the record that introduced the Killing Joke sound now marking its 46th anniversary this October.

items._cn_summary: 本文并非真正意义上的乐评，而是一篇关于Killing Joke首张同名专辑发行46周年的资讯回顾。文章梳理了专辑的录制背景、发行历程、曲目列表、封面设计来源，以及后续被Metallica、Helmet、Foo Fighters等乐队翻唱的记录。同时也简述了乐队从1978年组建到首张EP《Turn to Red》再到签约E.G. Records的过程。作为后朋克与工业摇滚的先驱之作，这张专辑在制作上强调现场同期录音、几乎不使用叠录，呈现出原始而直接的声响质感。其封面采用了Don McCullin拍摄的北爱尔兰德里CS气体冲突照片，政治隐喻强烈。Pitchfork将其列为史上最佳工业专辑第九位。整体内容以事实信息为主，缺乏对音乐本身的声音分析、美学探讨或主观评价。

items.body: Berlin-based darkwave act Night Nail released the single “Vile Train” on 2 October 2026 through Icy Cold Records. The track is the first digital single from the band’s forthcoming full-length album “Infinite Fountain,” set for release on 6 November 2026 through the same French label. A video for “Vile Train” accompanies the single. Night Nail’s Brandon Robert wrote “Vile Train” after a visit to the ash-covered ruins of Pompeii, Italy, where a Roman fresco depicting an angel and a demon locked in embrace became the song’s starting point. The lyrics follow two dreamers from separate realities who meet at the edge of their daydreams, fall into an obsession, and become trapped in a psychological cage of their own making. Robert describes the result as a “sonic assault of dark and brutal truths about love sung in a twisted but beautiful way.” “Vile Train” was mixed and post-produced by William Faith at 13 Studio in Chicago and co-produced by Night Nail in Berlin, with additional vocals and guitar by VV & the Void, the darkwave project of Berlin musician Valentina Veil. Watch the video for ‘Vile Train’ The official video for “Vile Train” is available on YouTube: Night Nail – ‘Vile Train’ (Official Video). ‘Infinite Fountain’ due 6 November “Infinite Fountain” is available for presale on Bandcamp ahead of its 6 November 2026 release through Icy Cold Records. “Vile Train” streams on Spotify. Infinite Fountain by Night Nail About Night Nail Night Nail was founded in Los Angeles in 2013 by Brandon Robert and Justin Deaktiviere. Michael Carpenter Jr. on guitar, David Cluff on bass and Bryan Panzeri on drums joined for the project’s early releases. The project is now based in Berlin, Germany. An early self-titled EP drew press, college radio and blog coverage across the US, Europe, South America and Australia. The band’s debut album, “LA Demons,” was released in July 2018 on Cleopatra Records. Its title draws on Dostoevsky’s novel “Demons.” The sophomore album, “March to Autumn,” followed on 15 October 2020 through Cold Transmission Music. Pete Burns of Kill Shelter co-produced, mixed and mastered the record. Touring and session musicians Valentina Veil, Ilja Gavrilenko and Manuel Wagner contributed additional parts. In September 2023, Night Nail released the single “Narcoleptic Dream Catcher,” the first taste of the album “Fates Explained” on Metropolis Records. The single reached the top five of the Deutsche Alternative Charts. The “Fates Explained” video single followed that November. In January 2024, the band released a video for “Cracks In My Heart,” with Luna De La Torre on vocals, and in July 2024 issued “Early Demons & Demos,” a 10th-anniversary edition of early material. “Vile Train,” released 2 October 2026 through Icy Cold Records, is the first single from “Infinite Fountain,” due 6 November 2026.
items._genre: darkwave / post-punk / gothic
items._cn_summary: Night Nail发布单曲《Vile Train》，为其即将推出的全长专辑《Infinite Fountain》的先行作品，由法国厂牌Icy Cold Records发行。主创Brandon Robert以意大利庞贝古城的灰烬废墟为灵感来源，从一幅描绘天使与恶魔相拥的罗马壁画出发，构筑出关于两个梦境者在各自幻想边界相遇、陷入执念并被自身心理牢笼困住的故事。制作层面，这首歌在柏林完成录音与共同制作，由芝加哥13 Studio的William Faith负责混音与后期制作，柏林音乐人Valentina Veil参与了额外人声与吉他录制。乐队如今以柏林为基地，早期在洛杉矶成立，自2013年以来陆续发表了多张专辑及EP，作品长期受到欧洲与美国地下暗潮场景的关注。

The five-track set gathers “Backstall,” “Sweat & Slit,” “Rust & Strobe,” “Concrete Fever” and “Swallow the Noise,” tagged as techno on the platform. The compilation is part of a wider opening catalog. Raveiac released five tracks on 2 October: “Concrete Fever,” “Bite the Wire,” “Just One More,” “Swallow the Noise” and “I Feed It.” Two more, “Rust & Strobe” and “Sweat & Slit,” followed on 3 October, and “Backstall” closed the run on 4 October, for eight tracks in three days. There is no Bandcamp page yet. The catalog streams exclusively through Raveiac’s SoundCloud profile. Raveiac’s own description connects the project to “industrial rave, hard techno, breakbeat, EBM, gabber and digital hardcore,” through what it calls “a direct punk vocabulary: repeated commands, physical hooks and lyrics shaped by concrete rooms, surveillance, machinery, appetite and loss of control.” The project’s SoundCloud bio reads in full: “Rave-punk from Turkey. Dirty industrial raves, broken breaks, and digital decay. Repost what hits. Push it deeper underground.” ‘Rust & Strobe’ and ‘Swallow the Noise’ Raveiac singled out two tracks from the set for press attention. “Rust & Strobe” opens on metallic percussion and broken drums and closes on what the project calls “an acid-charged chorus.” “Swallow the Noise” is described as a faster industrial-rave track carried by a chanted vocal line and distorted production. Raveiac also presents a visual identity drawn from photocopied zines, neon imagery, torn paper, halftone noise and analog damage. About Raveiac Raveiac launched in October 2026 as an independent rave-punk project from Turkey. Between 2 and 4 October 2026, the project released eight tracks on SoundCloud: “Concrete Fever,” “Bite the Wire,” “Just One More,” “Swallow the Noise” and “I Feed It” on 2 October, “Rust & Strobe” and “Sweat & Slit” on 3 October, and “Backstall” on 4 October. Five of those tracks, “Backstall,” “Sweat & Slit,” “Rust & Strobe,” “Concrete Fever” and “Swallow the Noise,” make up the compilation “Rave-Punk Rituals Vol. 1”.

items._cn_summary: 来自土耳其的新锐锐舞朋克项目 Raveiac 在 SoundCloud 一次性释出八首作品，其中五首汇编成首张合辑《Rave-Punk Rituals Vol. 1》。制作上横跨工业锐舞、硬核 techno、碎拍、EBM、gabber 与数字硬核等多种边缘电子类型，歌词以重复口号构建出直接的身体性钩子，主题围绕混凝土地下场景、监视、机器、欲望与失控。视觉系统借由霓虹、撕纸、半色调噪点与模拟损伤等复印杂志美学呈现，强化其地下身份。两首被单独推介的曲目——以金属打击乐与失真碎鼓开场、收束于酸性合唱段的《Rust & Strobe》，以及更快速、由呼喊式人声与扭曲制作驱动的工业锐舞曲《Swallow the Noise》——展示了项目对高强度舞曲语言的处理方式。整体呈现更偏向信息发布与项目介绍，缺乏对音乐内部结构与艺术价值的深度评析。

items.body: Out of all of the underrated bands I know, Boss Keloid have to be among the most underrated. They have many virtues I could sing but the main one is that they just sound like no one else. Their type of winding, dense, and uniquely harmonic stoner/progressive rock is just inimitable. And so, I live between Keloid to Keloid release, craving the very specific flavor that only they can provide. Happily, my latest fix is almost here and good lord is it glorious! Float & Aperture leaves behind a lot of the size and grandiosity of Family The Smiling Thrush and the density of Melted On the Inch in favor of a hard to pin down etherealness. "Pedestal", the second track which I am very pleased to premiere here, will do a better job at explaining what I mean than I can. Check it out below. Float & Aperture by Boss Keloid God, I just love this band. On "Pedestal" you get a taste of the leitmotif which runs through the entire album, some strangely (and pleasingly) sweet, high pitched vocals, and a whole lot of that sound palette that makes Boss Keloid who they are. Which is what exactly? It's that insidious lead guitar line, the fact that I could mean any of the three (at my count) lead guitar lines, the bubbling bass, the way the whole thing feels off-kilter, hazy, and psychedelic to such a unique degree. And finally, it's the excellent lyrics, here (like on the rest of the album) turned very introverted, musing on meaning, intent, self-knowledge, and failure.The entire release is this good. Like "Pedestal", it's angry at times. At others it's alluring, fantastical, strange, self-flagellating, self-aggrandizing, and a few dozens other emotions and perspectives besides. It's similar to previous Keloid releases but also different, uniquely its own thing just like all of their other albums. God I love this band. Please listen to this band! The full thing drops on October 23rd and you can, and should, pre-order it from the Bandcamp page above.
items._genre: stoner rock / progressive rock / psychedelic rock
items._cn_summary: 这张作品延续了乐队一贯的迷幻与前卫融合路线，但相比前作减少了宏大感和密度，转而追求一种难以归类的空灵氛围。以蜿蜒、致密且极具辨识度的吉他线条为核心，贝斯在其间低沉推进，合成高亢人声与器乐编织成失衡而迷幻的音景。歌词主题转向内省，涉及意义、意图、自我认知与挫败感的反复咀嚼，情绪在愤怒、诱惑、奇幻与自毁之间游走。作为小众乐队的小规模独立发行，该专辑在保持个人风格的同时展现出新的方向，但仍根植于stoner rock传统框架内，与用户偏好的实验爵士、电子及暗潮领域有一定距离。

items.tags: art sound art contemporary music improvisation
items.excerpt: 会期：2026/08/05 会場：京都芸術センター 講堂［京都府］ 公式サイト： https://www.kac.or.jp/events/260805/ （前編より） すでに見たように、本作『ジェローム・ベル』の構造の肝は、メタ・ダンスである自作についてのレクチャー・パフォーマンスであり、さらにそれ自体が何重にもねじれたメタ・ダンス性をもつ点にある。パリ・オペラ座バレエ団のバレリーナやマース・カニングハム舞踊団のダンサー、タイ古典舞踊のダンサーなど、「多様なバックグラウンドをもつダンサーが自身について語るドキュメンタリー作品」を制作してきた振付家が、自分自身にそのメソッドを適用しつつ、「本人ではない他者に自伝を語らせる」というねじれや矛盾。ベル自身は、気候変動対策がきっかけであったと述べるが、ここでは、ダンス（舞台芸術）が反復性・再現可能性を前提とすることそれ自体が俎上に乗せられている。 冒頭、舞台に登場した川口隆夫は、前説を述べ、机に座ってノートパソコンを開けると、「私はジェローム・ベルです」とおもむろに自己紹介を始める。「16歳の娘がいます」「今57歳です」「振付家です」。川口自
items.body: 会期：2026/08/05 会場：京都芸術センター 講堂［京都府］ 公式サイト： https://www.kac.or.jp/events/260805/ （前編より） すでに見たように、本作『ジェローム・ベル』の構造の肝は、メタ・ダンスである自作についてのレクチャー・パフォーマンスであり、さらにそれ自体が何重にもねじれたメタ・ダンス性をもつ点にある。パリ・オペラ座バレエ団のバレリーナやマース・カニングハム舞踊団のダンサー、タイ古典舞踊のダンサーなど、「多様なバックグラウンドをもつダンサーが自身について語るドキュメンタリー作品」を制作してきた振付家が、自分自身にそのメソッドを適用しつつ、「本人ではない他者に自伝を語らせる」というねじれや矛盾。ベル自身は、気候変動対策がきっかけであったと述べるが、ここでは、ダンス（舞台芸術）が反復性・再現可能性を前提とすることそれ自体が俎上に乗せられている。 冒頭、舞台に登場した川口隆夫は、前説を述べ、机に座ってノートパソコンを開けると、「私はジェローム・ベルです」とおもむろに自己紹介を始める。「16歳の娘がいます」「今57歳です」「振付家です」。川口自身も振付家としてダンス作品を創作しており（そのなかには、記録映像に基づいて大野一雄の舞踏を完コピする『大野一雄について』［2013］というメタ・ダンス的作品も含まれる）、年齢も近いが、川口は俳優のようにベルを演じているわけではなく、書かれたテキストを日本語で読み上げ、指定された箇所でパソコンを操作して映像を再生させている。舞台上で語られるのは、ダンスをめぐる自作の思索に加え、ダンスとの出会い、エイズによる親友の死、父親になった喜びなどの自伝的語りだが、ベル自身は舞台上には一切姿を現わさず、指定した台詞を他者にしゃべらせ、パソコンを操作させている。ここで顕現するのは、「他者の身体を遠隔操作する」というまさに振付の力学だ。観客は、振付家としてのベル自身についての語りを聞きながら、同時に「他者の身体に及ぼされている振付の作用」そのものを目撃する。 ［Documentation Team © 2026 Hot Summer in Kyoto］ ベル自身、常に「振付（家）という権力性」についてラディカルかつ自己言及的に問うてきたが、本作のタイトル『ジェローム・ベル』は、作品名であると同時に振付家としての署名・・でもある。言い換えれば、この作品は『川口隆夫』ではない。出演者が「その人自身であること」は限りなく希薄化し、消去される。本作は、振付家としての成功も失敗も赤裸々に語られ、失恋や子どもの成長を見守る喜びなど私的な側面も率直に語る、一見誠実なドキュメンタリーでありつつ、完全に非ドキュメンタリーでもある。ここには、「ドキュメンタリー・シアターははたしてどこまで成立可能なのか？」という矛盾した問いも内包されている。一方、本作では、ベル／川口の境界線がわずかに揺らぐ瞬間もある。90年代初めにエイズで友人を亡くしたことが語られるシーンでは、「ダムタイプ」に参加した経歴をもつ川口が、自身の過去を重ね合わせているような沈黙の間があった。 本作はまた、舞台作品の基盤にある反復性や代演可能性を問うとともに、映像アーカイブと舞台芸術の一回性をめぐる問題も内包する。作中では、ダンス作品がスペクタクルな消費社会の速度に抗う抵抗として、繰り返し「今、ここ」にいることの重要性が説かれる。一方、作中で抜粋映像が紹介される自作について、「全編はYoutubeで見れます」と何度も述べられる。「自作についての解説が、それ自体を裏切り、新たな問いを派生させる」という構造がここにもある。 レクチャー・パフォーマンスであり、多層的なメタ・ダンス作品であり、「ドキュメンタリー」の成立（不）可能性をめぐる問いであり、映像アーカイブと舞台のライブ性に対する問いでもある本作。最後に、「クレジット」にも施された仕掛けについて触れたい。「出演」は、川口隆夫だけではなく、「記録映像」で紹介された過去の自作に出演した人物の名前がすべて列挙され、長大なリストをなしている。ここには、「作品の出演者」とは誰を指すのか？ という問いかけとともに、「過去作品に出演した 彼ら全員・・・・とともにこの作品がある」という敬意と誠意が込められている。 鑑賞日：2026/08/05（水） 関連レビュー 未だ見ぬ身体へ──川口隆夫『大野一雄について』｜岡村恵子：フォーカス（2017年11月15日号） 川口隆夫ソロダンスパフォーマンス『大野一雄について』｜高嶋慈：artscapeレビュー（2015年12月15日号）

items._cn_summary: 本乐评讨论的是巴黎振付家Jérôme Bel的代表作『Jérôme Bel』2026年京都公演的后篇解析。作品由日本舞踊家川口隆夫登台，以「我是Jérôme Bel」为开场自述，在舞台上朗读文本、操作笔记本电脑播放影像，代为讲述Bel本人的自传，包括舞蹈缘起、友人因艾滋病去世、初为人父的喜悦等。乐评着重剖析此作的多重meta-dance结构：Bel将自身惯用的「为不同背景舞者拍摄纪录片」方法反转，让他人代述自己的自传；舞台上不见Bel本人，唯有他者身体承载着振付家的意志与文本，构成「远端操控他者身体」的振付力学本身的可视化。乐评亦触及反复性与代演可能性的悖论、YouTube影像档案与舞台现场性之间的张力，以及长串「出演者」名单对作品归属与集体劳动的致敬。

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. Find the artist online. Sara Serpa - Encounters and Collisions (Review) Karine Polwart- Laws of Motion (Review) Live in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, 2025

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑源于艺术家在爱丁堡皇家植物园的驻留项目，以园中最古老的标本——一棵2021年被砍伐的萨巴尔棕榈树为起点，展开关于自然、历史与传承的叙事。声音设计师与作曲家Pippa Murphy为作品加入精心的声景设计，配合Dave Milligan的钢琴，构筑出克制而富有亲密感的氛围。Karine Polwart温暖而富有同情心的嗓音成为核心载体，每首歌曲如同一次呼吸、一次记忆的回溯，既有手工艺般的庄重，又带有苏格兰民间音乐的根脉。开篇曲调的旋律如同一首缓慢、哀伤的挽歌，与风笛传统自然呼应。专辑在结尾揭示了反讽式的转折：两百年来被认定为Sabal bermudana的树种，实为Sabal mexicana，新的幼苗将在原地续写生命。这是一张以钢琴、人声与轻量声景编织的克制之作，以内省的方式呈现自然、时间与身份的宏大命题。

items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. Tako Toki - Un Dimanche � Monaco (Review) GuldGanger - GuldGanger (Review)

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.
