items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

Liz Harris of Grouper draws up the anchor of her 2013 slowcore side project and sets sail once more with drummer Jed Bindeman on the high seas Linda's Head by Helen On 27th March 1980 Mt. St Helens erupted. Two months later, Liz Harris (AKA Grouper) was born. In 2013, she teamed up with drummer Jed Bindeman and Scott Simmon on bass, introducing the world to their shoegaze band Helen with the double A-side single ‘Felt This Way’ / ‘Dying All The Time’. Their dreamy debut The Original Faces followed two years after with the band subsequently laying dormant… until now. The reappearance of this Pacific Northwest slowcore trio a decade later is less an eruption, more a profusion. Or, better... The post Helen – Linda’s Head appeared first on The Quietus.

items.body: Review by UMUR — "Section X" is the second full-length studio album by Danish power/progressive metal act BeyondTwilight (if you discount the two Twilight albums as the works of another band). The album wasreleased through Massacre Records in March 2005. It�s the successor to "The Devil's Hall of Fame"from 2001. The nucleus of the band is intact (namely keyboard player and band founder Finn Zierler,guitarist Anders Ericson Kragh, bassist Anders Lindgren, and drummer Tomas Fred�n) since the releaseof "The Devil's Hall of Fame" but there have been a couple of lineup changes. The omnipresent JacobHansen (Invocator, Anubis Gate, Pyramaze...etc.) has joined on guitars and vocals, and American leadvocalist Kelly Sundown Carpenter (Darkology, Inner Sanctum, Outworld...etc.) has replaced Norwegianvocalist J�rn Lande (Ark, Masterplan, Allen - Lande...etc.).Stylistically the material on "Section X" is a combination of epic power metal and heavy metaloriented progressive metal. The latter means that this is progressive oriented music but nottechnical for the sake of it, and you shouldn't expect long instrumental sections dominating thetracks. Beyond Twilight�s music is more song oriented and generally features relatively accessibleverse/chorus structures. The tracks are quite sophisticated though (listen to the almost theatrical"Sleeping Beauty"). The closest relative is to my ears Symphony X because of the power metal andprogressive metal hybrid style, but also because of the epic nature of the music, the heaviness ofthe music (this is not vanilla Euro power metal), and the omnipresence of keyboards. Carpenter isquite the impressive singer with a strong voice and commanding delivery and the musicianship isgenerally through the roof on this release."Section X" features a powerful, heavy, and detailed sound production. It�s polished and wellproduced but still heavy and raw enough not to become too sterile sounding. Every instrument andvocal part stand out in the mix and are perfectly balanced. Just because this is Zierler�s projectdoesn�t mean that the keyboards overshadow everything else. On the contrary Zierler is veryconscious in terms of when his keyboards should dominate a track and when they shouldn�t. Uponconclusion "Section X" is a step up in quality from the already great "The Devil's Hall of Fame" andit�s just through and through a high quality release from Beyond Twilight. A 4 - 4.5 star (85%)rating is deserved.(Originally posted on Metal Music Archives).
items._genre: progressive metal / power metal
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是丹麦力量前卫金属乐队Beyond Twilight的第二张录音室全长作品，由键盘手Finn Zierler创立的核心阵容保持稳定，并加入了吉他手Jacob Hansen和美国主唱Kelly Sundown Carpenter取代了此前的挪威主唱Jørn Lande。音乐风格融合了史诗力量金属和偏重金属化的前卫金属，歌曲结构以verse/chorus为主，偏向旋律可听性，但曲目本身相当复杂精细，部分作品如《Sleeping Beauty》带有戏剧化色彩。制作方面保持了厚重而精致的平衡，键盘并未过度压制其他乐器，乐手演奏水平整体很高。与Symphony X的风格有相似之处，被视为乐队前作的品质提升之作。评论本身信息量充足，分析角度专业，但音乐类型偏向主流化的金属风格，与用户偏好的实验前卫、爵士、电子、世界音乐及暗潮方向差距较大。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — There are times when reality is stranger than fiction, and the story behind the making of this album is another example of that. Philippe DeBarge was a young French heir to a pharmaceutical fortune and a huge fan of The Pretty Things. Guitarist Dick Taylor had become disillusioned by the lack of impact of S.F. Sorrow, leading Victor Unitt to join the band as his replacement; this was the first album he recorded with them. DeBarge contacted the musicians and invited them to his opulent ch�teau in Saint-Tropez to propose a deal: he would fund their stay and record an album with himself as the lead vocalist. There, at the Epi-Plage club and his own residence, a thoroughly bohemian gathering took place, reminiscent of a Fran�oise Sagan novel; French rock legend Johnny Hallyday and actress Brigitte Bardot mingled and played guitar amidst a black-and-white "Nouvelle Vague" atmosphere. The album was recorded in London at Nova Studios. Thanks to DeBarge's funding, The Pretty Things had access to high-quality equipment, including an 8-track tape recorder.After the recording sessions, DeBarge took the masters to France, and the material remained in storage, unreleased and forgotten, on acetate discs. The acetate has been bootlegged since then. In 2010, it was acquired by Mike Stax, owner of the 1960s music magazine Ugly Things. He unearthed one of the two acetates, had it mixed and mastered, and then, as a bonus track, It led the classic Pretty Things lineup, which Dick Taylor had just left at the time the tracks with DeBarge were recorded, to record a song titled "Monsieur Rock" (Philippe's Ballad) as a bonus track for this release on Ugly Things UTCD-2207.The songs "Alexander," "Eagle's Son," and "It'll Never Be Me" were already known, having been recorded in the late 1960s by "Electric Banana", the pseudonym under which The Pretty Things recorded soundtracks for De Wolfe Music. Notably, these three songs appear in Menahem Golan's film What's Good for the Goose (1969).The Philippe DeBarge album itself serves as a bridge between the group's major Works, S.F. Sorrow and Parachute, yet it stands on its own merits. Less dark than its predecessor, it is perhaps the final example of that fresh, unpredictable, exciting, and thrilling, yet fun, psychedelia. This is evident in the opening track, "Hello, How Do You Do," which echoes the trippier side of the Rolling Stones' Their Satanic Majesties era, while the restrained calm of "You Might Even Say" recalls the Kinks. The track "Alexandre" is vocally challenging, raw and pugnacious, reminiscent of the early Who, yet it takes flight thanks to the Pretty Things' backing vocals and Victor Unitt's diverse guitar solos; these solos explore various shades of psychedelia while occasionally channeling the wild spirit of his previous group, the Edgar Broughton Band.These tracks sit alongside others with a more pop-oriented sound, charming thanks to the use of the clavichord, as in "Send You With Loving," and a prominent bassline. The album's real strength lies in its garage-rock, almost proto-punk, tracks, which are packed with energy and vocal harmonies, blending acoustic Indian ethnic elements with rock 'n' roll piano, as heard in "You're Running You And Me." "Peace" possesses a unique poetry and beauty, and is linked to "Eagle's Son," carrying forward its infectious rhythm and energy. It features melodies full of personality, where the rock and pop of "Swinging London" float through, almost becoming anthems of the era.While the influence of the Beatles could be traced in FS Sorrow, here we find psychedelia driven by acoustic guitar and harpsichord, punctuated by bursts of distorted electric guitar in soundscapes closer to the Kinks. The work evokes an era when the past and the future did not clash, simply because they were distinct, as seen in "New Day." Wally Waller handles piano and organ duties on "It'll Never Be Me", a track that remains laid-back right up until Victor Unitt's screeching solo, while the bongo percussion adds a relaxing touch that contrasts with the album's more urgent moments."Monsieur Rock (Ballad Of Philippe)" sounds more modern yet fits the spirit perfectly; it is even moving, evoking an era where the backing vocals and guitar seem to pick up exactly where they left off. The sound is raw, defiant, and powerful, with an improvisational feel, making it a fitting tribute that brings a sense of currency and relevance to this long-awaited official release.Twink left in late 1969 to form Pink Fairies. Skip Alan returned on drums just in time for the band's return to Abbey Road to begin work on Parachute, which retained the psychedelic sound but incorporated increasingly progressive elements. And Philippe DeBarge shines like those teenage memories that, as time goes by, leave you wondering if they were real or imagined...distorted like that very psychedelia, a time capsule that endures like the eternally fair weather of the Saint-Tropez coast.
items._genre: psychedelic rock / proto-prog / 1960s rock
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑源于一段传奇故事：法国制药业继承人Philippe DeBarge资助The Pretty Things，邀请乐队前往其位于圣特罗佩的庄园，并在Nova Studios完成录音。录音母带长期以醋酸盘形式封存于法国，经杂志主理人Mike Stax发掘并重新混音后于2010年代发行。专辑定位为S.F. Sorrow与Parachute之间的过渡作品，收录多首为De Wolfe Music录制的影视配乐曲目。其音乐风格延续六十年代末迷幻摇滚脉络，开篇曲目呼应Rolling Stones的迷幻实验，而抒情段落则让人联想到The Kinks的克制内敛。Victor Unitt的多变吉他独奏在粗粝人声与乐队和声间穿插，呈现末期的英伦迷psychedelia面貌。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — Few late-80s metal albums are as influential as Savatage's fourth studio offering 'Hall of theMountain King', originally released by Atlantic. This is the first album by the American bandproduced by then-new producer Paul O'Neill, who had insisted on a more coherent musical direction,while also adding a bit of a conceptual edge to their recordings. At the same time, the band shows awillingness to experiment with more sophisticated arrangements and tighter compositions, as heardthroughout the album. The result is a darker, progressive-oriented record that sits at theintersection of melodic power metal and technical heavy metal, offering a triumphant and relentlesssound graced by fast-paced guitars and stunning vocal performances. As usual, fantastical elementsprevail on this Savatage album, bringing along an interesting aesthetic that sets the band apartfrom many of its contemporaries in the heavy metal scene. The lack of success of their previousalbums may have motivated Savatage to create a solid, kind of "bulletproof" collection of songs,that is what the record feels like.The straightforward songwriting, thunderous solos, and the overall dark atmosphere of 'Hall of theMountain King' render this album an appealing listen from start to finish. Its ten tracks areprimarily written by Jon and Criss Oliva, respectively lead singer and lead guitarist of the band,while a few songs also credit producer O'Neill as a co-writer. This record also has instrumentalarrangements of excerpts from 'In the Hall of the Mountain King' by Grieg and 'Mars, the Bringer ofWar' by Holst, which is further proof that Savatage were pursuing a sophistication of their soundwith this release. Opening side one is the song '24 Hrs. Ago'. Its sweeping, metallic riff providesa menacing and theatrical tone that is taken on by the following track 'Beyond the Doors of theDark', which is another really heavy and powerful composition. 'Legions' then explores a grooved uppower metal sound, while the melodic number 'Strange Wings' sees Savatage dialing back on the speedand aggression of the first three songs. Side two then follows up with the instrumental 'Prelude toMadness' and the iconic title track that needs no introduction. Of the four songs that follow andconclude the record, 'White Witch' and 'Devastation' impress as well-arranged ballsy metal pieces,while the instrumental interlude 'Last Dawn' is quite enjoyable. Of course, many of the progressiveelements are still underdeveloped on this release, while the instrumentals occasionally feel likestopgap entries in a sequence of songs mostly dedicated to powerful riffing and vocal bravado.Nevertheless, the vocals of Jon Oliva are fantastic all throughout 'Hall of the Mountain King',while the writing and the arrangements are really strong. The quality of the entire album isindicative of how Paul O'Neill understood what the band needed to become an 80s heavy metal majesty.And despite its minor imperfections, this 1987 record remains one of the most important entries inthe band's catalogue.
items._genre: progressive metal / power metal / heavy metal
items._cn_summary: 这张1987年的专辑是Savatage与新制作人Paul O'Neill合作的起点，呈现出更加连贯且具概念性的音乐方向。专辑将旋律性力量金属与技术性重金属相融合，以快速吉他riff、戏剧化编排和强烈的vocal表现为核心特征。Grieg《山魔王的宫殿》与Holst《火星》选段的器乐改编显示了乐队对古典素材的引用意图，但整体上仍以传统riff驱动的歌曲结构为主，进步元素被认为尚未充分发展。作为Atlantic厂牌发行的商业金属作品，制作精良但更倾向于主流重金属语法，对于偏好实验、前卫或电子路线的听众而言距离较远。

items.body:
Rolando Luna is bringing the sounds of Cuba to Singapore.

The former Buena Vista Social Club pianist will perform with his trio at Capitol Theatre on 30 November, blending Cuban musical traditions with jazz improvisation. Presented by Vamp Productions, Rolando Luna Trío: Soy Cuba… y Más! begins at 8PM, with doors opening at 7PM.

The trio’s repertoire spans original compositions, Cuban and American standards, boleros, and danzones. Fans can expect familiar melodies reworked through fresh arrangements and spontaneous exchanges, drawing on Luna’s grounding in Cuban rhythms, jazz, and classical music.

Winner of the 2007 Montreux Jazz piano competition, Luna has contributed to more than 200 albums. His career includes ten years performing with Buena Vista Social Club and two decades accompanying celebrated Cuban singer Omara Portuondo.

Luna began his musical journey at 15, studying at Havana’s Amadeo Roldán Conservatory before Portuondo selected him as an accompanist. Alongside their international performances, he has built his own body of work as a pianist, composer, and arranger.

The Singapore show is supported by the Embassy of Cuba in Singapore, with the Foundation for the Arts & Social Enterprise named as its charity beneficiary.

Early bird tickets are available until 14 October, 11:59PM SGT, with standard pricing taking effect on 15 October:

Seated, theatre-style free seating: SGD79 early bird / SGD88 standard

VIP Terrace: SGD124 early bird / SGD138 standard

Visit Vamp Productions’ event page for tickets and further details.

items.body: Review by VianaProghead — Review N� 990Frost* is a progressive rock band, a neo-prog super group that was formed in East Sussex, England, in 2004. Frost* was founded by songwriter, producer and musician Jem Godfrey, who is better known to the wider world for his work creating chart topping pop hits, when he made a conscious decision to return to his own musical past writing and playing progressive music. After writing and recording material on his own for several months and contacted several English well known musicians. Their debut studio work "Milliontown" was released in 2006. In 2008 they released their second one "Experiments In Mass Appeal". The third one "Falling Satellites" from 2016 will be the subject of the review.Although the band has remained true to the neo-prog style, the line up changes have brought some changes to the band's sound. The keyboards now play a more dominant role and since the guitar part has also been reduced, "Falling Satellites" seems smoother than its predecessors. It has little in common with "Milliontown", apart from the general style. "Experiments In Mass Appeal" gives a better indication of the direction. But with "Falling Satellites" Jem is still going one step further. Here we have nice prog and sophisticated pop with a lot of drive and a good feel for melodies with a catchy nature. The band seems genuine with a lot of fun with what they do presenting themselves confidently.So, "Falling Satellites" is the third studio album of Frost* and that was released in 2016. The line up on "Falling Satellites" is John Mitchell (vocals and guitar), Jem Godfrey (vocals, keyboards, electric and lap steel guitars and Chapman Stick), Nathan King (bass guitar) and Craig Blundell (drums). "Falling Satellites" also had the participation of Tori Beaumont (vocals), Joe Satriani (guitar) and Mark Knight (violin), all as guest artists."First Day" is a very short track. It begins the album with an ominous orchestration and a spacey ambience. It provides an atmospheric introduction that sets the ambient tone to the album. "Numbers" is a great track, an enjoyable rocker with a nice lilt to it that sets the upbeat tone of the album. It has a lot of depth and a lot going on. The vocals are layered perfectly on top of the instruments and backing tracks. "Towerblock" is easily the standout track on the album due to its level of experimentation and complete unconventionality within the scope of this sub-genre. It embraces their pop and electronic sensibilities and reflective lyrics into something that feels modern, but also classic. "Signs" has love lyrics with Mitchell on the lead vocals. This is arguably the most pop-oriented track we've heard from the band. It's another strong and heartfelt song that wouldn't sound out of place on either of their previous albums. "Lights Out" is a sort of ballad with pop infusions, a lovely tune with some great guest vocals by Tori singing along with Godfrey. It's a fantastic power ballad, a nice break in the middle of the album, to prepare us for the epic second half. "Heartstrings" is a solid rocker with great hooks and massive synthesisers. It oscillates between fiery futuristic hostility and calm, and the pop sensibilities. It has an ending that partially serves to transition into the following track. "Closer To The Sun" is more somber overall, a very dance-like track that brings the focus back around to the ambient pop vibes of "Lights Out". It's a track of beautiful, atmospheric and poppy post-rock, completed with great guitar and keyboard solos. "The Raging Against The Dying Of The Light Blues In 7/8" is the longest track on the album. It's full of energy outbursts and soft moments. It's a highly enjoyable hard rock song, energetic and captivating. It's a blistering track that should more than satisfy those looking for the pure prog on this album. "Nice Day For It..." is another dynamic and harmonically rich rocker. This is a real progressive rock track which contains certain musical elements you also hear on "First Day" and "Heartstrings". It's another track with some heavy "Milliontown" influence, being mostly instrumental. "Hypoventilate" suggests some kind of a sequel to "Hyperventilate" of "Milliontown". It's a very short track like "First Day". This is a transitional track that leads us into the last track. "Last Day" is a soft, lovely piece only containing vocals and piano. It obviously reimagines the sentiments of "First Day" to give the full-length a sense of meaningful conceptual continuity.Conclusion: With "Falling Satellites", Frost* has managed to create a beautiful and entertaining album that cannot really deny its pop origins. The basic ideas of the pieces and the melodies can often be imagined as pop songs, but it's an album that is progressive above all because of its clever mix. Godfrey proves himself to be a great producer and true keyboard wizard and he also cuts a good figure as a singer. Together with his top-class accompanists, he turns "Falling Satellites" into a real fantastic bundle of energy that can be described as an unexpected surprise coup. It's an exciting, always surprising album, on which there is a lot for prog lovers to discover, even if it can never really keep up with the two strong previous albums. It's undeniable that there is a pop influence on "Falling Satellites". In many ways, Frost* has once again redefined what is "modern" prog and they've done it with gusto and pomp and a smile on their faces.Prog is my Ferrari. Jem Godfrey (Frost*)

items._cn_summary: Frost* 是英国东萨塞克斯的neo-prog超级乐团，由Jem Godfrey于2004年创立，主创同时活跃于主流流行音乐制作领域。《Falling Satellites》是其第三张录音室专辑，乐队沿袭新前卫摇滚路线，但键盘比重明显提升，吉他部分有所削减，整体音色比前作更为柔和流畅。专辑融合了渐进摇滚结构与精致的流行元素，旋律朗朗上口，节奏充满推进感。客座音乐人包括Joe Satriani（吉他）和Mark Knight（小提琴）等。曲目方面，开场短曲以管弦乐铺陈氛围，'Numbers'展现活力摇滚底色，'Towerblock'被乐评视为专辑最出彩的实验性曲目，'Signs'与'Lights Out'则呈现更鲜明的流行化倾向，其中'Towerblock'在编排上体现了乐队对电子与流行元素的整合尝试。

items.body: Colossloth released a video for “Encoded Divinity” on 3 October 2026, a track from the album “The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites.” The album came out 2 October 2026 on Cold Spring Records, the project’s sixth release for the label. The video was produced by HAONDOKU Productions. The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites by Colossloth Watch the video for ‘Encoded Divinity’ The video is available on YouTube: COLOSSLOTH – ‘Encoded Divinity’ Promo Video. “Encoded Divinity” opens the album and runs 5:08. ‘The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites’ tracklist The album was announced in September with its full tracklist: “Encoded Divinity” (5:08) “Calculate Your Revolution” (7:00) “Awaiting MENA” (9:04) “Undertow Atlas” (10:34) “Only Adrift” (8:00) Cold Spring describes the album as centered on Theta Noir, a collective built around worship of Mena, a fictional artificial intelligence deity. The label calls the record “an automaton chant of cybernetic worship.” The album is available on CD in a matt-laminate digipak (catalogue number CSR375CD) through Cold Spring’s webstore, and for download via Bandcamp. Colossloth played an album launch show at The Globe in Glossop on 3 October 2026, alongside T.A.G.C. (Adi Newton of Clock DVA), Satøri and Llyn Y Cwn. Further dates follow on 7 November at St Anne’s in Barnstaple with Satøri and A Waste of Damnation, and from 27 to 29 November at Sheffield General Cemetery’s In The Black Midwinter event with The Golden Age of Doing Nothing and Decommissioned Forests. About Colossloth Colossloth is the solo project of Leicester, UK musician Wooly Woolaston, active since 2008. Woolaston has described Colossloth as “a one man Experimental Electronic artist where there are no rules to recording or playing music,” with a sound that has moved from long guitar drones toward harsher electronics with sections of melody. Woolaston released Colossloth’s first album through Doom Structure in 2008, followed by releases on Doom Mantra Records in 2009 and Dark Meadow Recordings in 2011. He later signed to Cold Spring Records, releasing “Anchored By Lungs” (2014), “Outstretch Your Hand for the Impress of Truth” (2015), “Heathen Needles” (2017), “Plague Alone” (2020) and “Promethean Meat” (2022), the latter incorporating drum samples and harsher rhythmic elements. Colossloth also appeared on the label’s “Arise – A Cold Spring Sampler” compilation alongside Coil, Merzbow and Mz.412, among others. Colossloth’s fifth Cold Spring album, “The Harmony Knife,” followed on 28 February 2025, a concept record drawing on Ted Kaczynski’s “Industrial Society and Its Future” and its argument for the psychological necessity of struggle, known as “the power process.” “The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites,” released 2 October 2026, is Colossloth’s sixth album for Cold Spring Records, now accompanied by a video for its opening track, “Encoded Divinity.”

items.body: Swedish duo Svaj. released a remix of the alan is waiting track “where you disappear” on 2 October 2026. The one-track single, titled “where you disappear (Svaj. Rebuild),” streams on Spotify and is available for download on Bandcamp and Subvert. The original song was written and sung by alan is waiting, the recording name of a Stockholm-based electronic artist whose debut album, “The Last of You,” came out in 2024. Svaj., the duo of Anders O Öhgren and Tomas Z Westberg based in Blackeberg, Stockholm, reworked the track for the remix. The release keeps alan is waiting’s original vocals. In a newsletter announcement, Svaj. described the result as “a wonky, New Order-tinged full-on synth-pop hit song.” where you disappear – Svaj. rebuild by Svaj., alan is waiting A visualizer for “where you disappear (Svaj. Rebuild)” is available on YouTube. About Svaj. Svaj. is the Stockholm duo of Anders O Öhgren and Tomas Z Westberg, based in the Blackeberg district of the city. The duo releases through its own TZW Produktion imprint. Svaj.’s Bandcamp profile describes its sound as “voice, electronics and bass. Minimal, experimental and industrial, yet melodic and danceable,” and compares it to Joy Division and Front 242. Svaj. issued its debut EP, “Rewind,” in March 2022. The songs reworked tracks originally recorded on tape in 1988, revisited with a Yamaha CS-10 synthesizer and a 1960s Tandberg reel-to-reel recorder. The duo’s second release, “Until We Fall,” followed in 2023. In 2024, Svaj. released the single “Cut Me Up,” a reworking of a song first written by Alien Waveform in 1989 and later issued as “Contagion” on the 1993 compilation “Tapping the Wires (A Selection of Futuristic Electro Mindbeats).” The digital single included a remix by UK industrial act Portion Control. The same year, Svaj. contributed “Brända Barn,” a reworking of a 1980 Swedish punk song, to the six-act compilation “SVÄRTA.” Svaj. released its third collection, “Maggots,” a six-track release, on 17 May 2025 through TZW Produktion on vinyl, CD and digital formats. The record includes a cover of John Cale’s 1974 track “Fear Is a Man’s Best Friend” and features contributions from Perra Wikström on contrabass and guitar and vocal effects from Devoid. Svaj. issued four music videos from “Maggots” through 2025, for “Experience,” “Fear,” “Portent” and, in October 2025, “Piglet.” The duo released the single “Patterns” on 19 February 2026. Svaj.’s catalog now runs from the 2022 “Rewind” EP through this month’s “where you disappear (Svaj. Rebuild)” remix.

items.body: Einstürzende Neubauten’s debut studio album, “Kollaps,” turns 45 this year. The German industrial band released the record on 5 October 1981 through the Hamburg label ZickZack. It remains the first official full-length release by Blixa Bargeld, N.U. Unruh and F.M. Einheit under the Einstürzende Neubauten name. “Kollaps” runs 38 minutes across eleven tracks, recorded in Berlin in 1981 and produced by the band itself. The album mixes rough punk-derived song structures with noise generated from self-built devices, electronics and metal plates and other found objects, a method that became the band’s signature. The tracklist includes “Tanz Debil,” “Steh auf Berlin,” “Negativ Nein,” “U-Haft Muzak,” “Draußen ist Feindlich,” “Schmerzen Hören (Hören mit Schmerzen),” “Jet’M” (a cover of Serge Gainsbourg’s “Je t’aime… moi non plus”), the title track “Kollaps,” “Sehnsucht,” “Vorm Krieg” and “Hirnsäge.” Later CD reissues appended additional tracks, including a live 1987 recording of “Negativ Nein.” Trouser Press described the record as “one of the most shocking visions ever committed to vinyl.” “Kollaps” is also listed in the reference book “1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die.” The album has since been reissued, including a 2002 edition paired with the 1982 dub companion “Stahldubversions.” About Einstürzende Neubauten Einstürzende Neubauten formed in Berlin in 1980 around vocalist and guitarist Blixa Bargeld and percussionist N.U. Unruh. The band’s name translates to “collapsing new buildings,” a reference to construction failures in West Berlin at the time. From the outset, the group built its sound around self-made and adapted instruments, including power tools, scrap metal, oil drums and construction debris, played alongside conventional guitar, bass and vocals. F.M. Einheit joined on percussion before the band’s first LP. The band’s earliest recorded appearance came via the cassette-only “Stahlmusik” in 1980. Einstürzende Neubauten signed to the Hamburg independent label ZickZack, which released “Kollaps” on 5 October 1981, the band’s first official studio album. The record was recorded in Berlin during 1981 and produced by the band itself, with no outside producer credited. Following “Kollaps,” Einstürzende Neubauten continued to record for European independent labels through the 1980s, including “Zeichnungen des Patienten O.T.” (1983) and the compilation “Strategies Against Architecture ’80-’83,” before moving to Some Bizzare/Mute for later releases. Bargeld also worked as a guitarist with Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds from the band’s formation in 1983. Einstürzende Neubauten’s lineup has changed over four decades, with Alexander Hacke and Marc Chung both joining in the years following “Kollaps.” The band added bassist Josefine Lukschy in 2026, alongside confirmed festival dates and studio webcasts. Forty-five years after “Kollaps” introduced the band’s self-made-instrument method on record, Einstürzende Neubauten remains active, with the album standing as the starting point of that catalogue.

items.body: Toronto-based guitarist, Ayal Senior, developed an approach of listening, playing and collaborating deeply, unhurried and with space (hence the title ‘Yutori‘, which translates to ‘space’) after several creative sojourns to Japan. This philosophy of taking time and patience to create comes through the record’s immeansly laid-back and tranquil dream-folk vibes. The album grew out of of a hushed winter morning session in the recording studio with Senior and several of his friends and collaborators leaning into this almost zen-like method of playing and being in tune with each other. The music’s vast openness and meditative qualities reflect the nature of these sessions, giving them the loose and communal feeling of tight improvised jams. This cooperative energy gives the record a sense of excitement, as it gives the impression the songs can go into any direction at any time. So your ear and attention are hooked right away, and they remain held til the needle reaches the deadwax on Side B. Throughout the album, you are treated to unique variations of instrumental ambient folk that splinters into cosmic string music and astral Americana sounds, with spacey pedal steel, acoustic and fried electric guitar, pearly vibraphones and warm cello. Some tracks are like mini-baroque symphonies, while others lean more into the psychedelic, with dreamlike atmospheric passages and stream of consciousness-styled distorted soloing. The record has the ambiance of a Nick Drake LP, but paired with the looseness and cosmic expansiveness of a Matt Valentine or even a Popol Vuh album. This is especially true with the track that finishes out Side A, “Well of Seven.” Yutori is as serene as a day spent floating around in a still pond, as pastoral as a walk through a freshly snow-covered forest and as illusory and wistful as a half-remembered daydream. If you need a bucolic and peaceful listen to soundtrack your autumn, then this is the album you should reach for. Click here to get your copy on vinyl or digital today. -KH
items._genre: ambient folk / dream-folk / psychedelic / cosmic Americana
items._cn_summary: 多伦多吉他手Ayal Senior受日本文化启发，以日语"余裕"（意为空间）为核心创作理念，在冬季录音室中与多位乐手即兴协作完成这张氛围民谣专辑。专辑强调留白与禅意，演奏方式松弛而冥想化，歌曲走向不可预测，营造出即兴jam的群体感。配器涵盖声学吉他、失真电吉他、空间感踏板钢棒琴、颤音琴与温暖大提琴，部分段落带有巴洛克交响曲气质，另一些则滑入迷幻氛围与意识流独奏。评论将其比作Nick Drake的内省气质与Matt Valentine、Popol Vuh的宇宙感开阔度的结合，呈现静谧池塘、雪后森林、半醒白日梦般的聆听体验。整体偏向梦幻民谣与迷幻原声路线，虽有即兴与跨界痕迹，但与用户偏好的实验、前卫、爵士、电子、世界音乐等核心领域距离较远。

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items.body: Review by Andis — Or, as it should probably have been called: The Endless Intro.Nobody needs to tell me this album is built from leftovers from previous sessions. After listeningto it, that fact practically introduces itself. In theory, recycling old material could have been agreat idea if anyone involved had possessed the energy, inspiration, or curiosity to actually dosomething interesting with it. Instead, the apparent creative process was: find some unused RichardWright keyboard recordings, sprinkle on a bit of guitar, drums, and the occasional mysteriousspaceship noise, then glue everything together and call it an album. Any questions?What makes this even more frustrating is that Pink Floyd is one of my favorite bands of all time.I've spent decades loving their music, so this isn't coming from a casual listener looking forsomething to complain about. If anything, I wanted to love this album more than anyone.Unfortunately, enthusiasm can only carry you so far when the music seems determined to driftaimlessly into the horizon.This record taught me an important life lesson: always listen before you buy. When I heard PinkFloyd were releasing a new album, I was so excited that I pre-ordered it immediately. That was amistake of truly Floydian proportions. I haven't been this bored since listening to The Final Cut.On the bright side, this album didn't make me quite as depressed, so I suppose that's progress.The Endless River is quite literally The Endless Intro. It feels like an introduction that somehowescaped containment and continued for over 52 minutes. If we're being generous, we can count thefinal track as an actual song, which brings the intro down to a mere 46 minutes. Was that song worthsitting through a 46-minute introduction? No. No, it was not.When you put the Pink Floyd name on an album, people naturally expect something resembling PinkFloyd. Not a 52-minute ambient soundscape that vaguely gestures toward Pink Floyd while offeringabsolutely nothing we haven't heard before, and usually heard done better. This is less a new albumand more a museum tour of discarded ideas.I'm giving it two stars, and that's me being charitable. There are a few pleasant moments scatteredthroughout the record, but they're buried beneath such a thick layer of mediocrity that excavatingthem feels like a part-time job.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Pink Floyd发行，取材自早前录音遗作，以Richard Wright的键盘素材为主干，叠加吉他、鼓机与太空音效，试图拼合成完整的概念作品。乐评人认为制作过程缺乏新意，整体如同一段不断延伸的前奏——长达五十二分钟的氛围声景，仅终曲勉强算得上歌曲，其余部分缺乏明确的结构与方向。作为资深乐迷，评论者对专辑抱有极高期待，预先订购后却大失所望，认为其只是旧素材的博物馆式陈列，未能展现任何新的创作意图。文中指出专辑在情绪上不如The Final Cut般令人沮丧，但同样令人感到乏味。评论人对最终曲目也不认可，认为不值得为它忍受四十六分钟无进展的引入。整体而言，乐评态度强烈负面，即使给出的两星评价也属宽容。

items.body: Independent Polish musician Sławek Stróżyk released the single “Tylko Ty” (“Only You”) on September 18, 2026, through distributor Crave Digital. The track places Polish-language male vocals in a synthwave/electro setting with a cyberpunk atmosphere, and explores closeness as a source of strength while the surrounding world changes. “Tylko Ty” runs 2 minutes and 47 seconds at 120 BPM. Stróżyk wrote the composition and lyrics, performed the track and handled its recording, production, mix and master himself in his home studio using Reaper. The original music and vocals involved no generative AI. “Tylko Ty” previously featured on the “Synthpop Symphony” podcast. The single is available to stream on Spotify, Apple Music and YouTube. About Sławek Stróżyk Sławek Stróżyk is an independent musician, composer, guitarist, vocalist and producer based in Poznań, Poland, with more than twenty years of experience spanning session performance, recording engineering and sound design. His solo work brings together synthwave and electronic production with a wider interest in pop, ballads and rock. Stróżyk records in his own home studio using Reaper, taking responsibility for the complete creative and technical process from composition through to the finished master. “Tylko Ty,” released September 18, 2026, is his latest single under that approach. Stróżyk is currently working on his debut solo album, with material spanning pop, ballads, rock and synthwave, continuing the independent, self-produced method behind “Tylko Ty.”

items.body: Los Angeles darkwave trio Chalice Sect released its first EP, “Finis Initii”, on September 25, 2026. The four-track release combines two new songs with two previously issued singles, among them “Silent Fever,” released in March 2026. The EP’s four tracks move between post-punk, EBM and dark electro. Its title translates from Latin as “the end of the beginning.” Daniel of Chalice Sect describes the release as closing the project’s early period: “Finis Initii – Latin for ‘the end of the beginning’ – represents the closing of the first chapter of Chalice Sect. The EP brings together the remaining songs I wrote during that period but had not yet released, alongside the two previously released singles. These tracks were written over the past few years and belong to an earlier phase of the project, both creatively and sonically. Bringing them together on this release gives that era a proper conclusion while creating space for what comes next: a newer sound and perhaps a different direction for Chalice Sect.” Finis Initii by Chalice Sect The tracklist runs “Fire in the Sound,” “Silent Fever,” “Take Me There Parts I & II” and “Undefined.” “Finis Initii” is available as a digital release on Bandcamp and Spotify. About Chalice Sect Chalice Sect is a Los Angeles darkwave trio. The band released its debut single, “Violet Grey,” on January 20, 2026, followed by “Silent Fever” that March. “Finis Initii,” issued September 25, 2026 as the band’s first EP, gathers the project’s new and previously released material from that period into a single release. Press materials for “Finis Initii” cite Twin Tribes, Kontravoid, She Past Away and Molchat Doma as reference points for the band’s sound.

items.body: M[SSΛNGR, the synthwave and darkwave project of Waukegan, Illinois musician Angelo Ochoa, released the single “Cycle” on 25 September 2026 through the label Anti-Joy. The track pairs synthwave and darkwave production with a modern pop song structure. Ochoa describes the results as “cinematic anthems.” “Cycle” was added to the Spotify curator playlist “Synthchronization: Sparkling Synths Take Over” following its release. The single streams on Spotify and is available across Apple Music, Deezer, Amazon Music, Tidal and SoundCloud. Ochoa states that no AI is involved in the production of his music. “Cycle” is the first single from Ochoa’s planned 15-track project “Evolution,” currently in production. Teaser clips for the project are scheduled to roll out through autumn 2026. About M[SSΛNGR M[SSΛNGR is the recording name of Angelo Ochoa, a musician based in Waukegan, Illinois, near Chicago. Ochoa writes and produces alone, combining synthwave and darkwave influences with pop song structures. “Cycle,” released through Anti-Joy on 25 September 2026, is the project’s first released single and the opening piece of the planned 15-track project “Evolution.”

items.body:
Creepy Nuts brought Japanese hip-hop to the National Stadium, opening the Singapore leg of The Weeknd’s After Hours Til Dawn Tour with a set of anime favourites, club beats and turntable flourishes.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Creepy Nuts (@creepynuts_official)

Rapper R-Shitei and DJ Matsunaga make a compelling double act. R-Shitei packs his verses with quick, tightly controlled syllables, while Matsunaga cuts into the beats with scratches and rhythmic accents. Their sound gives the ear plenty to follow: the pace of the rapping, the shifting percussion and the hooks that emerge from all that activity.

‘Biriken’ opened the set with a bouncing Jersey club rhythm, followed by ‘Yofukashi no Uta’ and the jazzy ‘Daten’. The mood grew darker with ‘doppelgänger’ and ‘Chxxai’, whose pounding beats and electronic textures brought the selection closer to a late-night club set.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Creepy Nuts (@creepynuts_official)

A dedicated DJ routine gave Matsunaga the spotlight midway through. Scratching, quick cuts and beat juggling are central to his performance style, making the decks an instrument with their own rhythmic voice. The placement gave both halves of the partnership their due before the instantly recognisable ‘Bling-Bang-Bang-Born’.

From there, the duo moved through ‘Mirage’, ‘Fright’ and ‘Nidone’, saving ‘Otonoke’ for last. The DAN DA DAN opening theme was a crowd favourite, rounding off their energetic set before The Weeknd took the stage.
